1→"""Read-only git observation with graceful degradation."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import logging
     6→import subprocess
     7→from dataclasses import dataclass
     8→
     9→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    10→
    11→_GIT_TIMEOUT = 5
    12→
    13→
    14→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    15→class GitContext:
    16→    available: bool
    17→    branch: str | None = None
    18→    head_sha: str | None = None
    19→    has_uncommitted: bool = False
    20→    root: str | None = None
    21→
    22→
    23→def detect_git_context() -> GitContext:
    24→    """Detect current git context (branch, HEAD, uncommitted changes).
    25→
    26→    Returns ``available=False`` when git is missing or not in a repo.
    27→    """
    28→    try:
    29→        head = subprocess.run(
    30→            ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    31→            capture_output=True,
    32→            text=True,
    33→            timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT,
    34→        )
    35→        if head.returncode != 0:
    36→            return GitContext(available=False)
    37→
    38→        sha = head.stdout.strip()[:12]
    39→
    40→        branch_result = subprocess.run(
    41→            ["git", "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"],
    42→            capture_output=True,
    43→            text=True,
    44→            timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT,
    45→        )
    46→        branch = branch_result.stdout.strip() if branch_result.returncode == 0 else None
    47→
    48→        root_result = subprocess.run(
    49→            ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
    50→            capture_output=True,
    51→            text=True,
    52→            timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT,
    53→        )
    54→        root = root_result.stdout.strip() if root_result.returncode == 0 else None
    55→
    56→        status_result = subprocess.run(
    57→            ["git", "status", "--porcelain"],
    58→            capture_output=True,
    59→            text=True,
    60→            timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT,
    61→        )
    62→        has_uncommitted = bool(status_result.stdout.strip()) if status_result.returncode == 0 else False
    63→
    64→        return GitContext(
    65→            available=True,
    66→            branch=branch,
    67→            head_sha=sha,
    68→            has_uncommitted=has_uncommitted,
    69→            root=root,
    70→        )
    71→    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as exc:
    72→        logger.debug("git context unavailable: %s", exc)
    73→        return GitContext(available=False)
    74→
    75→
    76→def update_pr_body(pr_number: int, body: str) -> bool:
    77→    """Update PR description via ``gh pr edit``.  Returns True on success."""
    78→    try:
    79→        result = subprocess.run(
    80→            ["gh", "pr", "edit", str(pr_number), "--body", body],
    81→            capture_output=True,
    82→            text=True,
    83→            timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT * 3,
    84→        )
    85→        if result.returncode != 0:
    86→            logger.warning("gh pr edit failed: %s", result.stderr.strip())
    87→            return False
    88→        return True
    89→    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as exc:
    90→        logger.warning("gh pr edit unavailable: %s", exc)
    91→        return False
    92→
    93→
    94→__all__ = ["GitContext", "detect_git_context", "update_pr_body"]
    95→

    38→  show       Dig into issues by file/dir/detector/ID
    39→  tree       Annotated codebase tree (zoom with --focus)
    40→  viz        Interactive HTML treemap
    41→  detect     Run a single detector directly (bypass state)
    42→
    43→improve:
    44→  autofix    Auto-fix mechanical issues
    45→  suppress   Suppress issues matching a pattern
    46→  exclude    Exclude path pattern from scanning
    47→  move       Move file/dir and update import references
    48→  review     Holistic subjective review (LLM-based)
    49→
    50→configure:
    51→  zone       Show/set zone classifications
    52→  config     Project configuration
    53→  langs      List language plugins
    54→  dev        Developer utilities
    55→  update-skill  Install/update agent skill document
    56→
    57→examples:
    58→  desloppify scan
    59→  desloppify scan --skip-slow --profile ci
    60→  desloppify plan                        # full prioritized markdown
    61→  desloppify plan queue                  # compact table of all items
    62→  desloppify next --count 10             # top 10 queue items
    63→  desloppify show src/components/Modal.tsx
    64→  desloppify plan resolve "unused::src/foo.tsx::React" \\
    65→    --note "removed import" --attest "I have actually ..."
    66→  desloppify review --run-batches --parallel --scan-after-import
    67→"""
    68→
    69→
    70→class _NoAbbrevArgumentParser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    71→    """Argparse parser variant that disables long-option abbreviation."""
    72→
    73→    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
    74→        kwargs.setdefault("allow_abbrev", False)
    75→        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
    76→
    77→
    78→def _cli_version_string() -> str:
    79→    """Return the best available CLI version label."""
    80→    try:
    81→        return f"desloppify {get_version('desloppify')}"
    82→    except PackageNotFoundError:
    83→        return "desloppify (version unknown)"
    84→
    85→
    86→def create_parser(*, langs: list[str], detector_names: list[str]) -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    87→    """Build top-level CLI parser with all subcommands."""
    88→    lang_help = ", ".join(langs) if langs else "registered languages"
    89→
    90→    parser = _NoAbbrevArgumentParser(
    91→        prog="desloppify",
    92→        description="Desloppify — codebase health tracker",
    93→        epilog=USAGE_EXAMPLES,
    94→        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    95→    )
    96→    parser.add_argument(
    97→        "--lang",
    98→        type=str,
    99→        default=None,
   100→        help=f"Language to scan ({lang_help}). Auto-detected if omitted.",
   101→    )
   102→    parser.add_argument(
   103→        "--exclude",
   104→        action="append",
   105→        default=None,
   106→        metavar="PATTERN",
   107→        help="Path pattern to exclude (component/prefix match; repeatable)",
   108→    )
   109→    parser.add_argument(
   110→        "--version",
   111→        "-V",
   112→        action="version",
   113→        version=_cli_version_string(),
   114→    )
   115→    sub = parser.add_subparsers(
   116→        dest="command",
   117→        required=True,
   118→        parser_class=_NoAbbrevArgumentParser,
   119→    )
   120→    # workflow
   121→    _add_scan_parser(sub)
   122→    _add_status_parser(sub)
   123→    _add_next_parser(sub)
   124→    _add_plan_parser(sub)
   125→    # investigate
   126→    _add_show_parser(sub)
   127→    _add_tree_parser(sub)
   128→    _add_viz_parser(sub)
   129→    _add_detect_parser(sub, detector_names)
   130→    # improve
   131→    _add_fix_parser(sub, langs)
   132→    _add_suppress_parser(sub)
   133→    _add_exclude_parser(sub)
   134→    _add_move_parser(sub)
   135→    _add_review_parser(sub)
   136→    # configure
   137→    _add_zone_parser(sub)
   138→    _add_config_parser(sub)
   139→    _add_langs_parser(sub)
   140→    _add_dev_parser(sub)
   141→    _add_update_skill_parser(sub)
   142→    return parser
   143→
   144→
   145→__all__ = ["USAGE_EXAMPLES", "create_parser"]

     2→

    10→
    11→class FileTextCache:
    12→    """Optional read-through file-text cache used by scan/review passes."""
    13→
    14→    def __init__(self) -> None:
    15→        self._enabled = False
    16→        self._values: dict[str, str | None] = {}
    17→
    18→    def enable(self) -> None:
    19→        self._enabled = True
    20→        self._values.clear()
    21→
    22→    def disable(self) -> None:
    23→        self._enabled = False
    24→        self._values.clear()
    25→
    26→    def read(self, filepath: str) -> str | None:
    27→        if self._enabled and filepath in self._values:
    28→            return self._values[filepath]
    29→
    30→        try:
    31→            content = Path(filepath).read_text(errors="replace")
    32→        except OSError:
    33→            content = None
    34→        if self._enabled:
    35→            self._values[filepath] = content
    36→        return content
    37→
    38→
    39→class SourceFileCache:
    40→    """Small FIFO cache for source-file discovery results."""
    41→
    42→    def __init__(self, *, max_entries: int) -> None:
    43→        self.max_entries = max_entries
    44→        self.values: dict[tuple, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
    45→
    46→    def get(self, key: tuple) -> tuple[str, ...] | None:
    47→        return self.values.get(key)
    48→
    49→    def put(self, key: tuple, value: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
    50→        if len(self.values) >= self.max_entries:
    51→            self.values.pop(next(iter(self.values)))
    52→        self.values[key] = value
    53→
    54→    def clear(self) -> None:
    55→        self.values.clear()
    56→
    57→
    58→@dataclass
    59→class RuntimeContext:
    60→    """Mutable runtime container for exclusion and cache state."""
    61→
    62→    exclusions: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    63→    project_root: Path | None = None
    64→    query_file: Path | None = None
    65→    file_text_cache: FileTextCache = field(default_factory=FileTextCache)
    66→    cache_enabled: bool = False
    67→    source_file_cache: SourceFileCache = field(
    68→        default_factory=lambda: SourceFileCache(max_entries=16)
    69→    )
    70→
    71→

    73→_RUNTIME_CONTEXT: ContextVar[RuntimeContext | None] = ContextVar(
    74→    "desloppify_runtime_context",
    75→    default=None,
    76→)
    77→
    78→
    79→def make_runtime_context(*, source_file_cache_max_entries: int = 16) -> RuntimeContext:
    80→    """Create an isolated runtime context."""
    81→    return RuntimeContext(
    82→        source_file_cache=SourceFileCache(max_entries=source_file_cache_max_entries)
    83→    )
    84→
    85→
    86→def current_runtime_context() -> RuntimeContext:
    87→    """Return the active runtime context (or process fallback)."""
    88→    runtime = _RUNTIME_CONTEXT.get()
    89→    if runtime is not None:

    91→    return _PROCESS_RUNTIME_CONTEXT

    24→def command_runtime(args) -> CommandRuntime:

1→"""Text-oriented utility helpers split from the main utils facade."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import os
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→
     8→from desloppify.base.runtime_state import current_runtime_context
     9→
    10→_DEFAULT_PROJECT_ROOT = Path(os.environ.get("DESLOPPIFY_ROOT", Path.cwd())).resolve()
    11→
    12→
    13→def get_project_root() -> Path:
    14→    """Return the active project root, checking RuntimeContext first.
    15→
    16→    Tests set ``RuntimeContext.project_root`` to point at a tmp directory.
    17→    Production code uses the process-level default from $DESLOPPIFY_ROOT / cwd.
    18→    """
    19→    override = current_runtime_context().project_root
    20→    if override is not None:
    21→        return override
    22→    return _DEFAULT_PROJECT_ROOT
    23→
    24→
    25→def read_code_snippet(
    26→    filepath: str,
    27→    line: int,
    28→    context: int = 1,
    29→    *,
    30→    project_root: Path | str | None = None,
    31→) -> str | None:
    32→    """Read ±context lines around a line number. Returns formatted string or None."""
    33→    try:
    34→        root = (
    35→            Path(project_root).resolve()
    36→            if project_root is not None
    37→            # Runtime-aware default; preserves RuntimeContext/project-root overrides.
    38→            else get_project_root()
    39→        )
    40→        full = Path(filepath)
    41→        if not full.is_absolute():
    42→            full = root / full
    43→        content = full.read_text(errors="replace")
    44→    except OSError:
    45→        return None
    46→    lines = content.splitlines()
    47→    if line < 1 or line > len(lines):
    48→        return None
    49→    start = max(0, line - 1 - context)
    50→    end = min(len(lines), line + context)
    51→    parts = []
    52→    for i in range(start, end):
    53→        ln = i + 1
    54→        marker = "→" if ln == line else " "
    55→        text = lines[i]
    56→        if len(text) > 120:
    57→            text = text[:117] + "..."
    58→        parts.append(f"    {marker} {ln:>4} │ {text}")
    59→    return "\n".join(parts)
    60→
    61→
    62→def get_area(filepath: str, *, min_depth: int = 2) -> str:
    63→    """Derive an area name from a file path (generic: first 2 path components).
    64→
    65→    *min_depth* controls the minimum number of path components required before
    66→    the two-component area is returned.  The default (2) means a path like
    67→    ``"a/b"`` already qualifies.  Python uses ``min_depth=3`` so that
    68→    ``"pkg/mod.py"`` returns just ``"pkg"`` while ``"pkg/sub/mod.py"`` returns
    69→    ``"pkg/sub"``.
    70→    """
    71→    text = (filepath or "").strip()
    72→    if not text:
    73→        return "(unknown)"
    74→    parts = Path(text).parts
    75→    if not parts:
    76→        return "(unknown)"
    77→    return "/".join(parts[:2]) if len(parts) >= min_depth else parts[0]
    78→
    79→
    80→def _consume_escaped_char(text: str, index: int, out: list[str]) -> int | None:
    81→    if text[index] != "\\" or index + 1 >= len(text):
    82→        return None
    83→    out.append(text[index : index + 2])
    84→    return index + 2
    85→
    86→
    87→def _skip_comment(text: str, index: int) -> int | None:
    88→    if text[index] != "/" or index + 1 >= len(text):
    89→        return None
    90→    next_char = text[index + 1]
    91→    if next_char == "/":
    92→        newline_at = text.find("\n", index)
    93→        return -1 if newline_at == -1 else newline_at
    94→    if next_char == "*":
    95→        end = text.find("*/", index + 2)
    96→        return -1 if end == -1 else end + 2
    97→    return None
    98→
    99→
   100→def strip_c_style_comments(text: str) -> str:
   101→    """Strip // and /* */ comments while preserving string literals."""
   102→    result: list[str] = []
   103→    i = 0
   104→    in_str = None
   105→    while i < len(text):
   106→        ch = text[i]
   107→        if in_str:
   108→            escaped_next = _consume_escaped_char(text, i, result)
   109→            if escaped_next is not None:
   110→                i = escaped_next
   111→                continue
   112→            if ch == in_str:
   113→                in_str = None
   114→            result.append(ch)
   115→            i += 1
   116→            continue
   117→
   118→        if ch in ('"', "'", "`"):
   119→            in_str = ch
   120→            result.append(ch)
   121→            i += 1
   122→            continue
   123→
   124→        skipped_to = _skip_comment(text, i)
   125→        if skipped_to is not None:
   126→            if skipped_to == -1:
   127→                break
   128→            i = skipped_to
   129→            continue
   130→
   131→        result.append(ch)
   132→        i += 1
   133→    return "".join(result)
   134→
   135→
   136→def is_numeric(value: object) -> bool:
   137→    """Return True if *value* is an int or float but NOT a bool.
   138→
   139→    Python's ``bool`` is a subclass of ``int``, so ``isinstance(True, int)``
   140→    is ``True``.  Many JSON-derived payloads need to distinguish real numbers
   141→    from booleans; this helper centralises that guard.
   142→    """
   143→    return isinstance(value, int | float) and not isinstance(value, bool)
   144→
   145→

   148→    "get_project_root",
   149→    "is_numeric",
   150→    "read_code_snippet",
   151→    "strip_c_style_comments",
   152→]

    54→
    55→def _mark_stale_on_mechanical_change(
    56→    state: StateModel,
    57→    *,
    58→    changed_detectors: set[str],
    59→    now: str,
    60→) -> None:
    61→    """Mark subjective assessments stale when mechanical issues change.
    62→
    63→    Only marks dimensions that already have an assessment — doesn't create
    64→    new entries for dimensions that have never been reviewed.
    65→    """
    66→    assessments = state.get("subjective_assessments")
    67→    if not isinstance(assessments, dict) or not assessments:
    68→        return
    69→
    70→    affected_dims: set[str] = set()
    71→    for detector in changed_detectors:
    72→        dims = _DETECTOR_SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSIONS.get(detector, ())
    73→        affected_dims.update(dims)
    74→
    75→    if not affected_dims:
    76→        return
    77→
    78→    for dimension in sorted(affected_dims):
    79→        if dimension not in assessments:
    80→            continue
    81→        payload = assessments[dimension]
    82→        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
    83→            continue
    84→        # Don't overwrite if already stale
    85→        if payload.get("needs_review_refresh"):
    86→            continue
    87→        payload["needs_review_refresh"] = True
    88→        payload["refresh_reason"] = "mechanical_issues_changed"
    89→        payload["stale_since"] = now

   125→    _merge_scan_inputs(
   126→        state,
   127→        lang=resolved_options.lang,
   128→        potentials=resolved_options.potentials,
   129→        merge_potentials=resolved_options.merge_potentials,
   130→        codebase_metrics=resolved_options.codebase_metrics,
   131→    )
   132→
   133→    existing = state["issues"]
   134→    ignore_patterns = (
   135→        resolved_options.ignore
   136→        if resolved_options.ignore is not None
   137→        else state.get("config", {}).get("ignore", [])
   138→    )
   139→    current_ids, new_count, reopened_count, current_by_detector, ignored_count, upsert_changed = (
   140→        upsert_issues(
   141→            existing,
   142→            current_issues,
   143→            ignore_patterns,
   144→            now,
   145→            lang=resolved_options.lang,
   146→        )
   147→    )
   148→
   149→    raw_issues = len(current_issues)
   150→    suppressed_pct = _compute_suppression(raw_issues, ignored_count)
   151→
   152→    ran_detectors = (
   153→        set(resolved_options.potentials.keys())
   154→        if resolved_options.potentials is not None
   155→        else None
   156→    )
   157→    suspect_detectors = find_suspect_detectors(
   158→        existing,
   159→        current_by_detector,
   160→        resolved_options.force_resolve,
   161→        ran_detectors,
   162→    )
   163→    auto_resolved, skipped_other_lang, resolved_out_of_scope, resolve_changed = auto_resolve_disappeared(
   164→        existing,
   165→        current_ids,
   166→        suspect_detectors,
   167→        now,
   168→        lang=resolved_options.lang,
   169→        scan_path=resolved_options.scan_path,
   170→        exclude=resolved_options.exclude,
   171→    )
   172→
   173→    # Mark subjective assessments stale when mechanical issues changed.
   174→    changed_detectors = upsert_changed | resolve_changed
   175→    if changed_detectors:
   176→        _mark_stale_on_mechanical_change(
   177→            state, changed_detectors=changed_detectors, now=now,
   178→        )
   179→
   180→    _recompute_stats(
   181→        state,
   182→        scan_path=resolved_options.scan_path,
   183→        subjective_integrity_target=resolved_options.subjective_integrity_target,
   184→    )
   185→    _append_scan_history(
   186→        state,
   187→        now=now,
   188→        lang=resolved_options.lang,
   189→        new_count=new_count,
   190→        auto_resolved=auto_resolved,
   191→        ignored_count=ignored_count,
   192→        raw_issues=raw_issues,
   193→        suppressed_pct=suppressed_pct,
   194→        ignore_pattern_count=len(ignore_patterns),
   195→    )
   196→
   197→    chronic_reopeners = [
   198→        issue
   199→        for issue in existing.values()
   200→        if issue.get("reopen_count", 0) >= 2 and issue["status"] == "open"
   201→    ]
   202→
   203→    validate_state_invariants(state)
   204→    return _build_merge_diff(
   205→        new_count=new_count,
   206→        auto_resolved=auto_resolved,
   207→        reopened_count=reopened_count,
   208→        current_ids=current_ids,
   209→        suspect_detectors=suspect_detectors,
   210→        chronic_reopeners=chronic_reopeners,
   211→        skipped_other_lang=skipped_other_lang,
   212→        resolved_out_of_scope=resolved_out_of_scope,
   213→        ignored_count=ignored_count,
   214→        ignore_pattern_count=len(ignore_patterns),
   215→        raw_issues=raw_issues,
   216→        suppressed_pct=suppressed_pct,
   217→    )

   203→def matches_target_score(

1→"""Tool metadata helpers (hashing, staleness checks)."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import hashlib
     6→import logging
     7→from pathlib import Path
     8→
     9→from desloppify.base.output.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
    10→
    11→TOOL_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    12→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    13→
    14→
    15→def _compute_tool_hash_with_diagnostics(
    16→    *,
    17→    tool_dir: Path | None = None,
    18→) -> tuple[str, int]:
    19→    """Compute tool hash and unreadable-file count."""
    20→    active_tool_dir = tool_dir or TOOL_DIR
    21→    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    22→    unreadable_files = 0
    23→    for py_file in sorted(active_tool_dir.rglob("*.py")):
    24→        rel_parts = py_file.relative_to(active_tool_dir).parts
    25→        if "tests" in rel_parts:
    26→            continue
    27→        try:
    28→            digest.update(str(py_file.relative_to(active_tool_dir)).encode())
    29→            digest.update(py_file.read_bytes())
    30→        except OSError as exc:
    31→            unreadable_files += 1
    32→            log_best_effort_failure(
    33→                logger,
    34→                f"read tool-hash source file {py_file}",
    35→                exc,
    36→            )
    37→            digest.update(f"[unreadable:{py_file.name}]".encode())
    38→            continue
    39→    return digest.hexdigest()[:12], unreadable_files
    40→
    41→
    42→def compute_tool_hash(*, tool_dir: Path | None = None) -> str:
    43→    """Compute a content hash of all .py files in the desloppify package."""
    44→    digest, _ = _compute_tool_hash_with_diagnostics(tool_dir=tool_dir)
    45→    return digest
    46→
    47→
    48→def check_tool_staleness(state: dict, *, tool_dir: Path | None = None) -> str | None:
    49→    """Return warning if tool code has changed since last scan."""
    50→    stored = state.get("tool_hash")
    51→    if not stored:
    52→        return None
    53→    current, unreadable_files = _compute_tool_hash_with_diagnostics(tool_dir=tool_dir)
    54→    if current != stored:
    55→        suffix = (
    56→            f" ({unreadable_files} unreadable file(s) encountered while hashing)"
    57→            if unreadable_files > 0
    58→            else ""
    59→        )
    60→        return (
    61→            f"Tool code changed since last scan (was {stored}, now {current}){suffix}. "
    62→            "Scores will refresh on next scan"
    63→        )
    64→    if unreadable_files > 0:
    65→        return (
    66→            f"Tool hash check completed with {unreadable_files} unreadable file(s); "
    67→            "staleness verification may be incomplete."
    68→        )
    69→    return None
    70→
    71→
    72→_NEEDS_RESCAN_WARNING = (
    73→    "Config changed — scores may be stale. Run: desloppify scan"
    74→)
    75→
    76→
    77→def check_config_staleness(config: dict) -> str | None:
    78→    """Return warning if config changes have invalidated cached scores."""
    79→    if config.get("needs_rescan"):
    80→        return _NEEDS_RESCAN_WARNING
    81→    return None
    82→
    83→

    85→    "TOOL_DIR",
    86→    "check_config_staleness",
    87→    "check_tool_staleness",
    88→    "compute_tool_hash",

1→"""Runtime state model for exclusions and in-memory caches."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from contextlib import contextmanager
     6→from contextvars import ContextVar
     7→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→
    10→
    11→class FileTextCache:
    12→    """Optional read-through file-text cache used by scan/review passes."""
    13→
    14→    def __init__(self) -> None:
    15→        self._enabled = False
    16→        self._values: dict[str, str | None] = {}
    17→
    18→    def enable(self) -> None:
    19→        self._enabled = True
    20→        self._values.clear()
    21→
    22→    def disable(self) -> None:
    23→        self._enabled = False
    24→        self._values.clear()
    25→
    26→    def read(self, filepath: str) -> str | None:
    27→        if self._enabled and filepath in self._values:
    28→            return self._values[filepath]
    29→
    30→        try:
    31→            content = Path(filepath).read_text(errors="replace")
    32→        except OSError:
    33→            content = None
    34→        if self._enabled:
    35→            self._values[filepath] = content
    36→        return content
    37→
    38→
    39→class SourceFileCache:
    40→    """Small FIFO cache for source-file discovery results."""
    41→
    42→    def __init__(self, *, max_entries: int) -> None:
    43→        self.max_entries = max_entries
    44→        self.values: dict[tuple, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
    45→
    46→    def get(self, key: tuple) -> tuple[str, ...] | None:
    47→        return self.values.get(key)
    48→
    49→    def put(self, key: tuple, value: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
    50→        if len(self.values) >= self.max_entries:
    51→            self.values.pop(next(iter(self.values)))
    52→        self.values[key] = value
    53→
    54→    def clear(self) -> None:
    55→        self.values.clear()
    56→
    57→
    58→@dataclass
    59→class RuntimeContext:
    60→    """Mutable runtime container for exclusion and cache state."""
    61→
    62→    exclusions: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    63→    project_root: Path | None = None
    64→    query_file: Path | None = None
    65→    file_text_cache: FileTextCache = field(default_factory=FileTextCache)
    66→    cache_enabled: bool = False
    67→    source_file_cache: SourceFileCache = field(
    68→        default_factory=lambda: SourceFileCache(max_entries=16)
    69→    )
    70→
    71→
    72→_PROCESS_RUNTIME_CONTEXT = RuntimeContext()
    73→_RUNTIME_CONTEXT: ContextVar[RuntimeContext | None] = ContextVar(
    74→    "desloppify_runtime_context",
    75→    default=None,
    76→)
    77→
    78→
    79→def make_runtime_context(*, source_file_cache_max_entries: int = 16) -> RuntimeContext:
    80→    """Create an isolated runtime context."""
    81→    return RuntimeContext(
    82→        source_file_cache=SourceFileCache(max_entries=source_file_cache_max_entries)
    83→    )
    84→
    85→
    86→def current_runtime_context() -> RuntimeContext:
    87→    """Return the active runtime context (or process fallback)."""
    88→    runtime = _RUNTIME_CONTEXT.get()
    89→    if runtime is not None:
    90→        return runtime
    91→    return _PROCESS_RUNTIME_CONTEXT
    92→
    93→
    94→@contextmanager
    95→def runtime_scope(runtime: RuntimeContext | None = None):
    96→    """Run code with an isolated runtime context."""
    97→    active = runtime or make_runtime_context()
    98→    [REDACTED](active)
    99→    try:
   100→        yield active
   101→    finally:
   102→        _RUNTIME_CONTEXT.reset(token)
   103→
   104→

   106→    "FileTextCache",

   108→    "SourceFileCache",
   109→    "current_runtime_context",
   110→    "make_runtime_context",

   112→]

    46→def _primary_lang_from_issues(issues: dict) -> str | None:
    47→    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    48→    for issue in issues.values():
    49→        if not isinstance(issue, dict):

    51→        raw_lang = issue.get("lang")
    52→        if not isinstance(raw_lang, str) or not raw_lang.strip():

    83→def _compute_dimension_score(

    86→    """Compute (score, pass_rate, assessment_score) for a dimension."""
    87→    assessment_score = (
    88→        max(0.0, min(100.0, float(assessment.get("score", 0))))
    89→        if isinstance(assessment, dict)
    90→        else 0.0
    91→    )
    92→    integrity_penalty = (
    93→        assessment.get("integrity_penalty")
    94→        if isinstance(assessment, dict)
    95→        else None
    96→    )
    97→    reset_pending = bool(
    98→        isinstance(assessment, dict)
    99→        and (
   100→            assessment.get("reset_by") == "scan_reset_subjective"
   101→            or assessment.get("source") == "scan_reset_subjective"
   102→            or assessment.get("placeholder") is True
   103→        )
   104→    )
   105→    if reset_pending:
   106→        score = 0.0
   107→        pass_rate = 0.0
   108→    elif integrity_penalty == "target_match_reset":
   109→        score = 0.0
   110→        pass_rate = 0.0
   111→    elif has_assessment:
   112→        score = assessment_score
   113→        pass_rate = score / 100.0
   114→    else:
   115→        score = 0.0
   116→        pass_rate = 0.0
   117→    return score, pass_rate, assessment_score

   120→def _extract_components(assessment: dict) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, float]]:
   121→    """Extract component names and scores from an assessment dict."""
   122→    components: list[str] = []
   123→    component_scores: dict[str, float] = {}
   124→    raw_components = assessment.get("components")
   125→    if isinstance(raw_components, list):
   126→        components = [
   127→            str(item).strip()
   128→            for item in raw_components
   129→            if isinstance(item, str) and item.strip()
   130→        ]
   131→    raw_component_scores = assessment.get("component_scores")
   132→    if isinstance(raw_component_scores, dict):

   134→            if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():

   136→            if not is_numeric(value):

   138→            component_scores[key.strip()] = round(

   140→                1,
   141→            )
   142→    return components, component_scores
   143→
   144→
   145→def append_subjective_dimensions(
   146→    results: dict,
   147→    issues: dict,
   148→    assessments: dict | None,
   149→    failure_set: frozenset[str],
   150→    allowed_dimensions: set[str] | None = None,
   151→) -> None:
   152→    """Append subjective review dimensions to results dict (mutates results).
   153→
   154→    Subjective scoring is evidence-first: open review issues for a dimension
   155→    determine pass-rate, while imported assessment scores are retained as
   156→    metadata for transparency.
   157→    """
   158→    raw_defaults = DIMENSIONS
   159→    allowed = (
   160→        {_normalize_dimension_key(name) for name in allowed_dimensions}
   161→        if allowed_dimensions is not None
   162→        else None
   163→    )
   164→
   165→    default_dimensions = []
   166→    for raw_dim in raw_defaults:
   167→        dim = _normalize_dimension_key(raw_dim)
   168→        if not dim:
   169→            continue
   170→        if allowed is not None and dim not in allowed:
   171→            continue
   172→        default_dimensions.append(dim)
   173→
   174→    assessed: dict[str, dict] = {}
   175→    for raw_dim, payload in (assessments or {}).items():
   176→        dim = _normalize_dimension_key(raw_dim)
   177→        if not dim:
   178→            continue
   179→        # Real assessments (from review imports) always count regardless of
   180→        # allowed_dimensions — they were deliberately imported and should not
   181→        # be silently discarded.  However, system-generated placeholders
   182→        # (scan_reset_subjective) are not real assessments and should respect
   183→        # the allowed_dimensions scope like defaults.
   184→        is_placeholder = isinstance(payload, dict) and (
   185→            payload.get("placeholder") is True
   186→            or payload.get("source") == "scan_reset_subjective"
   187→            or payload.get("reset_by") == "scan_reset_subjective"
   188→        )
   189→        if is_placeholder and allowed is not None and dim not in allowed:
   190→            continue
   191→        assessed[dim] = payload
   192→    existing_lower = {k.lower() for k in results}
   193→    lang_name = _primary_lang_from_issues(issues)
   194→
   195→    all_dims = list(default_dimensions)
   196→    for dim_name in assessed:
   197→        if dim_name not in default_dimensions:
   198→            all_dims.append(dim_name)
   199→
   200→    for dim_name in all_dims:
   201→        is_default = dim_name in default_dimensions
   202→        assessment = assessed.get(dim_name)
   203→        has_assessment = isinstance(assessment, dict)
   204→        if not is_default and not assessment:
   205→            continue
   206→
   207→        display = _dimension_display_name(dim_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   208→        if display.lower() in existing_lower:
   209→            display = f"{display} (subjective)"
   210→
   211→        # Count open review/concern issues for display (work queue), but
   212→        # these do NOT drive the dimension score — only assessment scores do.
   213→        issue_count = sum(
   214→            1
   215→            for issue in issues.values()
   216→            if issue.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   217→            and issue.get("status") in failure_set
   218→            and _normalize_dimension_key(
   219→                issue.get("detail", {}).get("dimension")
   220→            )
   221→            == dim_name
   222→        )
   223→
   224→        score, pass_rate, assessment_score = _compute_dimension_score(
   225→            assessment, has_assessment,
   226→        )
   227→        reset_pending = bool(
   228→            isinstance(assessment, dict)
   229→            and (
   230→                assessment.get("reset_by") == "scan_reset_subjective"
   231→                or assessment.get("source") == "scan_reset_subjective"
   232→                or assessment.get("placeholder") is True
   233→            )
   234→        )
   235→        components: list[str] = []
   236→        component_scores: dict[str, float] = {}
   237→        if isinstance(assessment, dict):
   238→            components, component_scores = _extract_components(assessment)
   239→
   240→        results[display] = {
   241→            "score": round(float(score), 1),
   242→            "tier": 4,
   243→            "checks": SUBJECTIVE_CHECKS,
   244→            "failing": issue_count,
   245→            "detectors": {
   246→                "subjective_assessment": {
   247→                    "potential": SUBJECTIVE_CHECKS,
   248→                    "pass_rate": round(pass_rate, 4),
   249→                    "failing": issue_count,
   250→                    "weighted_failures": round(SUBJECTIVE_CHECKS * (1 - pass_rate), 4),
   251→                    "assessment_score": round(assessment_score, 1),
   252→                    "placeholder": reset_pending or not has_assessment,
   253→                    "dimension_key": dim_name,
   254→                    "configured_weight": round(
   255→                        _dimension_weight(dim_name, lang_name=lang_name), 6
   256→                    ),
   257→                    "components": components,
   258→                    **(
   259→                        {"component_scores": component_scores}
   260→                        if component_scores
   261→                        else {}
   262→                    ),
   263→                }
   264→            },
   265→        }
   266→
   267→
   268→__all__ = [
   269→    "DISPLAY_NAMES",
   270→    "append_subjective_dimensions",
   271→]
   272→

    10→from desloppify.languages._framework import (
    11→    discovery,

    16→from desloppify.languages._framework.base.types import LangConfig
    17→from desloppify.languages._framework.contract_validation import validate_lang_contract
    18→from desloppify.languages._framework.policy import REQUIRED_DIRS, REQUIRED_FILES

    25→from desloppify.languages._framework.structure_validation import validate_lang_structure
    26→
    27→T = TypeVar("T")
    28→
    29→
    30→def register_lang(name: str) -> Callable[[T], T]:
    31→    """Decorator to register a language config class.
    32→
    33→    Validates structure, instantiates the class, validates the contract,
    34→    and stores the *instance* in the registry.
    35→    """
    36→
    37→    def decorator(cls: T) -> T:
    38→        module = inspect.getmodule(cls)
    39→        if module and hasattr(module, "__file__"):
    40→            validate_lang_structure(Path(module.__file__).parent, name)
    41→        if isinstance(cls, type) and issubclass(cls, LangConfig):
    42→            cfg = make_lang_config(name, cls)  # instantiate + validate
    43→            registry_state.register(name, cfg)  # store instance
    44→        else:
    45→            registry_state.register(name, cls)  # test doubles
    46→        return cls
    47→
    48→    return decorator
    49→
    50→
    51→def register_generic_lang(name: str, cfg: LangConfig) -> None:
    52→    """Register a pre-built language plugin instance (no package structure required)."""
    53→    validate_lang_contract(name, cfg)
    54→    registry_state.register(name, cfg)
    55→
    56→
    57→def reload_lang_plugins() -> list[str]:
    58→    """Force plugin rediscovery and return refreshed language names."""
    59→    discovery.load_all(force_reload=True)
    60→    return sorted(registry_state.all_keys())
    61→

   162→    )
   163→    if narrative.get("milestone"):
   164→        print(colorize(f"  → {narrative['milestone']}", "green"))
   165→
   166→    next_command = _print_next_command(state)
   167→    _write_resolve_query_entry(

   169→            patterns=args.patterns,

   178→            narrative=narrative,
   179→            state=state,

   261→        fallback = cls._clone_default(default)
   262→        if raw is None:
   263→            return fallback

   274→                return fallback

   276→                return bool(raw)

   278→

   280→            if isinstance(raw, bool):
   281→                return fallback
   282→            if _is_numeric(raw):

   292→            if _is_numeric(raw):

   294→            try:

   297→                return fallback
   298→
   299→        if expected is str:
   300→            return raw if isinstance(raw, str) else str(raw)
   301→
   302→        if expected is list:
   303→            return raw if isinstance(raw, list) else fallback
   304→
   305→        if expected is dict:

   307→

   310→    def normalize_settings(self, values: dict[str, object] | None) -> dict[str, object]:
   311→        values = values if isinstance(values, dict) else {}
   312→        normalized: dict[str, object] = {}
   313→        for key, spec in self.setting_specs.items():
   314→            raw = values.get(key, spec.default)
   315→            normalized[key] = self._coerce_value(raw, spec.type, spec.default)
   316→        return normalized

   318→    def normalize_runtime_options(
   319→        self,
   320→        values: dict[str, object] | None,
   321→        *,
   322→        strict: bool = False,
   323→    ) -> dict[str, object]:
   324→        values = values if isinstance(values, dict) else {}
   325→        specs = self.runtime_option_specs
   326→        if strict:
   327→            unknown = sorted(set(values) - set(specs))
   328→            if unknown:
   329→                raise KeyError(
   330→                    f"Unknown runtime option(s) for {self.name}: {', '.join(unknown)}"
   331→                )
   332→        normalized: dict[str, object] = {}
   333→        for key, spec in specs.items():
   334→            raw = values.get(key, spec.default)
   335→            normalized[key] = self._coerce_value(raw, spec.type, spec.default)
   336→        return normalized

   347→        if options is not None:

   122→def cmd_scan(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   123→    """Run all detectors, update persistent state, show diff."""

   130→        print_lang_runtime_options_error(exc, lang_name=lang_name)
   131→        raise SystemExit(2) from exc

   133→        print(colorize(f"  {exc}", "red"))
   134→        raise SystemExit(2) from exc

   136→        runtime,

   141→    )

1→"""Shared regex policies for migration/auth signal detection."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import re
     6→
     7→DEPRECATION_MARKER_RE = re.compile(r"@[Dd]eprecated\b|DEPRECATED", re.MULTILINE)
     8→
     9→MIGRATION_TODO_RE = re.compile(
    10→    r"(?:TODO|FIXME|HACK)\b(?:\s*:)?[^\n]*\b(?:migrat\w*|legacy|deprecat\w*|old.?api|remove.?after)\b",
    11→    re.IGNORECASE,
    12→)
    13→
    14→SERVICE_ROLE_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(
    15→    r"\b(?:service[_-]?role(?:_key)?|serviceRole(?:Key)?|SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE(?:_KEY)?)\b",
    16→    re.IGNORECASE,
    17→)
    18→
    19→SERVER_ONLY_PATH_HINTS = (
    20→    "/api/",
    21→    "/server/",
    22→    "/backend/",
    23→    "/functions/",
    24→    "/supabase/functions/",
    25→    "/scripts/",
    26→)
    27→
    28→
    29→def is_server_only_path(path: str) -> bool:
    30→    """Best-effort classification for server-only source paths."""
    31→    if not path:
    32→        return False
    33→    normalized = path.replace("\\", "/")
    34→    prefixed = normalized if normalized.startswith("/") else f"/{normalized}"
    35→    return any(hint in prefixed for hint in SERVER_ONLY_PATH_HINTS)
    36→

   247→    """Configure metadata providers for subjective-dimension lookups."""
   248→    state = _PROVIDER_STATE

   251→    if (
   252→        available_languages_provider is not None
   253→        and available_languages_provider is not state.available_languages_provider

   348→            lang_defaults, lang_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(name)
   349→            _merge_dimension_meta(
   350→                out,
   351→                dimensions=lang_defaults,
   352→                prompts=lang_prompts,
   353→                override_existing=bool(lang_name),
   354→            )
   355→        except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   356→            logger.debug("Failed to load dimensions for lang %s: %s", name, exc)
   357→            continue
   358→
   359→    for dim, payload in out.items():
   360→        payload.setdefault(
   361→            "display_name",
   362→            _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.get(dim, _title_display_name(dim)),
   363→        )
   364→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   365→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   366→        if dim in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES:
   367→            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
   368→        else:
   369→            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   370→
   371→    # Preserve legacy dimensions even if a payload temporarily drops one.
   372→    for dim, display in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.items():
   373→        payload = out.setdefault(dim, {})
   374→        payload.setdefault("display_name", display)
   375→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   376→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", True)
   377→        payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
   378→
   379→    return out
   380→
   381→
   382→@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
   383→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata() -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   384→    """Return merged metadata across all known dimensions/languages."""
   385→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=None)
   386→
   387→
   388→@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
   389→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(
   390→    lang_name: str | None,
   391→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   392→    """Return merged metadata for one language (with language overrides)."""
   393→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   394→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=normalized)
   395→
   396→
   397→def _metadata_registry(lang_name: str | None) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   398→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   399→    if normalized is None:
   400→        return load_subjective_dimension_metadata()
   401→    return load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(normalized)
   402→
   403→
   404→def get_dimension_metadata(
   405→    dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None
   406→) -> dict[str, object]:
   407→    """Return metadata for one dimension key (with sane defaults)."""
   408→    dim = _normalize_dimension_name(dimension_name)
   409→    all_meta = _metadata_registry(lang_name)
   410→    payload = dict(all_meta.get(dim, {}))
   411→
   412→    payload.setdefault("display_name", _title_display_name(dim))
   413→    payload.setdefault("weight", 1.0)
   414→    payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   415→    payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   416→    return payload
   417→
   418→
   419→def dimension_display_name(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> str:
   420→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   421→    return str(meta.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dimension_name)))
   422→
   423→
   424→def dimension_weight(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> float:
   425→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   426→    raw = meta.get("weight", 1.0)
   427→    if is_numeric(raw):
   428→        return max(0.0, float(raw))
   429→    return 1.0
   430→
   431→
   432→def default_display_names_map(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
   433→    """Display-name map for default subjective dimensions."""
   434→    out: dict[str, str] = {}
   435→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   436→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   437→            continue
   438→        out[dim] = str(payload.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dim)))
   439→    return out
   440→
   441→
   442→def resettable_default_dimensions(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   443→    """Default subjective dimensions that should be reset by scan reset."""
   444→    out = []
   445→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   446→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   447→            continue
   448→        if not bool(payload.get("reset_on_scan", True)):
   449→            continue
   450→        out.append(dim)
   451→    return tuple(sorted(set(out)))
   452→
   453→
   454→__all__ = [
   455→    "DISPLAY_NAMES",
   456→    "configure_subjective_dimension_providers",
   457→    "default_dimension_keys",

   459→    "default_display_names_map",
   460→    "dimension_display_name",
   461→    "dimension_weight",
   462→    "get_dimension_metadata",

   464→    "load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang",
   465→    "reset_subjective_dimension_providers",
   466→    "resettable_default_dimensions",
   467→]

   401→    """Return a compact action type label for a dimension based on its detectors."""
   402→    best = "manual"
   403→    best_pri = 99
   404→    for d in DETECTORS.values():
   405→        if d.dimension == dim_name:
   406→            pri = _ACTION_PRIORITY.get(d.action_type, 99)
   407→            if pri < best_pri:

   410→    return _ACTION_LABELS.get(best, "manual")

   254→    @staticmethod
   255→    def _clone_default(default: object) -> object:
   256→        return copy.deepcopy(default)
   257→
   258→    @classmethod
   259→    def _coerce_value(cls, raw: object, expected: type, default: object) -> object:
   260→        """Best-effort coercion for config/CLI values."""
   261→        fallback = cls._clone_default(default)
   262→        if raw is None:
   263→            return fallback
   264→
   265→        if expected is bool:
   266→            if isinstance(raw, bool):
   267→                return raw
   268→            if isinstance(raw, str):
   269→                lowered = raw.strip().lower()
   270→                if lowered in {"1", "true", "yes", "on"}:
   271→                    return True
   272→                if lowered in {"0", "false", "no", "off"}:
   273→                    return False
   274→                return fallback
   275→            if _is_numeric(raw):
   276→                return bool(raw)
   277→            return fallback
   278→
   279→        if expected is int:
   280→            if isinstance(raw, bool):
   281→                return fallback
   282→            if _is_numeric(raw):
   283→                return int(raw)
   284→            try:
   285→                return int(raw)
   286→            except (TypeError, ValueError):
   287→                return fallback
   288→
   289→        if expected is float:
   290→            if isinstance(raw, bool):
   291→                return fallback
   292→            if _is_numeric(raw):
   293→                return float(raw)
   294→            try:
   295→                return float(raw)
   296→            except (TypeError, ValueError):
   297→                return fallback
   298→
   299→        if expected is str:
   300→            return raw if isinstance(raw, str) else str(raw)
   301→
   302→        if expected is list:
   303→            return raw if isinstance(raw, list) else fallback
   304→
   305→        if expected is dict:
   306→            return raw if isinstance(raw, dict) else fallback
   307→
   308→        return raw if isinstance(raw, expected) else fallback
   309→
   310→    def normalize_settings(self, values: dict[str, object] | None) -> dict[str, object]:
   311→        values = values if isinstance(values, dict) else {}
   312→        normalized: dict[str, object] = {}
   313→        for key, spec in self.setting_specs.items():
   314→            raw = values.get(key, spec.default)
   315→            normalized[key] = self._coerce_value(raw, spec.type, spec.default)
   316→        return normalized
   317→
   318→    def normalize_runtime_options(
   319→        self,
   320→        values: dict[str, object] | None,
   321→        *,
   322→        strict: bool = False,
   323→    ) -> dict[str, object]:
   324→        values = values if isinstance(values, dict) else {}
   325→        specs = self.runtime_option_specs
   326→        if strict:
   327→            unknown = sorted(set(values) - set(specs))
   328→            if unknown:
   329→                raise KeyError(
   330→                    f"Unknown runtime option(s) for {self.name}: {', '.join(unknown)}"
   331→                )
   332→        normalized: dict[str, object] = {}
   333→        for key, spec in specs.items():
   334→            raw = values.get(key, spec.default)
   335→            normalized[key] = self._coerce_value(raw, spec.type, spec.default)
   336→        return normalized
   337→
   338→    def set_runtime_context(
   339→        self,
   340→        *,
   341→        settings: dict[str, object] | None = None,
   342→        options: dict[str, object] | None = None,
   343→    ) -> None:
   344→        """Set default runtime settings/options for future LangRun creation."""
   345→        if settings is not None:
   346→            self._default_runtime_settings = self.normalize_settings(settings)
   347→        if options is not None:
   348→            self._default_runtime_options = self.normalize_runtime_options(options)
   349→
   350→    def runtime_setting(self, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
   351→        """Read setting from config-level runtime defaults."""
   352→        if key in self._default_runtime_settings:
   353→            return copy.deepcopy(self._default_runtime_settings[key])
   354→        spec = self.setting_specs.get(key)
   355→        if spec:
   356→            return copy.deepcopy(spec.default)
   357→        return default
   358→
   359→    def runtime_option(self, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
   360→        """Read option from config-level runtime defaults."""
   361→        if key in self._default_runtime_options:
   362→            return copy.deepcopy(self._default_runtime_options[key])
   363→        spec = self.runtime_option_specs.get(key)
   364→        if spec:
   365→            return copy.deepcopy(spec.default)
   366→        return default
   367→
   368→    def detect_lang_security_detailed(
   369→        self,
   370→        files: list[str],
   371→        zone_map: FileZoneMap | None,
   372→    ) -> LangSecurityResult:
   373→        """Language-specific security checks with optional coverage metadata."""
   374→        return LangSecurityResult(entries=[], files_scanned=0)

   377→        self, graph: dict, zone_map: FileZoneMap | None
   378→    ) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   379→        """Language-specific private-import detection. Override in subclasses."""
   380→        return [], 0

   384→        return []

   268→            if isinstance(raw, str):
   269→                lowered = raw.strip().lower()
   270→                if lowered in {"1", "true", "yes", "on"}:
   271→                    return True
   272→                if lowered in {"0", "false", "no", "off"}:
   273→                    return False
   274→                return fallback
   275→            if _is_numeric(raw):
   276→                return bool(raw)
   277→            return fallback
   278→
   279→        if expected is int:
   280→            if isinstance(raw, bool):
   281→                return fallback
   282→            if _is_numeric(raw):
   283→                return int(raw)
   284→            try:
   285→                return int(raw)
   286→            except (TypeError, ValueError):
   287→                return fallback
   288→
   289→        if expected is float:
   290→            if isinstance(raw, bool):
   291→                return fallback
   292→            if _is_numeric(raw):
   293→                return float(raw)
   294→            try:
   295→                return float(raw)
   296→            except (TypeError, ValueError):
   297→                return fallback
   298→
   299→        if expected is str:
   300→            return raw if isinstance(raw, str) else str(raw)
   301→
   302→        if expected is list:
   303→            return raw if isinstance(raw, list) else fallback
   304→
   305→        if expected is dict:
   306→            return raw if isinstance(raw, dict) else fallback
   307→
   308→        return raw if isinstance(raw, expected) else fallback

   310→    def normalize_settings(self, values: dict[str, object] | None) -> dict[str, object]:
   311→        values = values if isinstance(values, dict) else {}
   312→        normalized: dict[str, object] = {}
   313→        for key, spec in self.setting_specs.items():
   314→            raw = values.get(key, spec.default)
   315→            normalized[key] = self._coerce_value(raw, spec.type, spec.default)
   316→        return normalized

   318→    def normalize_runtime_options(
   319→        self,
   320→        values: dict[str, object] | None,
   321→        *,
   322→        strict: bool = False,
   323→    ) -> dict[str, object]:
   324→        values = values if isinstance(values, dict) else {}
   325→        specs = self.runtime_option_specs
   326→        if strict:
   327→            unknown = sorted(set(values) - set(specs))
   328→            if unknown:
   329→                raise KeyError(
   330→                    f"Unknown runtime option(s) for {self.name}: {', '.join(unknown)}"
   331→                )
   332→        normalized: dict[str, object] = {}
   333→        for key, spec in specs.items():
   334→            raw = values.get(key, spec.default)
   335→            normalized[key] = self._coerce_value(raw, spec.type, spec.default)
   336→        return normalized

   342→        options: dict[str, object] | None = None,

   345→        if settings is not None:

   347→        if options is not None:
   348→            self._default_runtime_options = self.normalize_runtime_options(options)

   351→        """Read setting from config-level runtime defaults."""
   352→        if key in self._default_runtime_settings:
   353→            return copy.deepcopy(self._default_runtime_settings[key])
   354→        spec = self.setting_specs.get(key)
   355→        if spec:
   356→            return copy.deepcopy(spec.default)
   357→        return default

   363→        spec = self.runtime_option_specs.get(key)
   364→        if spec:

   366→        return default

   239→        for ds in (entry.get("dimension_scores") or {}).values():

   244→def ensure_state_defaults(state: StateModel | dict) -> None:
   245→    """Normalize loose/legacy state payloads to a valid base shape in-place."""
   246→    migrate_state_keys(state)
   247→

   256→        state["scan_history"] = []

   259→    if not isinstance(state.get("score_confidence"), dict):

   261→    if not isinstance(state.get("subjective_integrity"), dict):
   262→        state["subjective_integrity"] = {}
   263→
   264→    all_issues = state["issues"]
   265→    to_remove: list[str] = []
   266→    for issue_id, issue in all_issues.items():
   267→        if not isinstance(issue, dict):
   268→            to_remove.append(issue_id)
   269→            continue
   270→
   271→        issue.setdefault("id", issue_id)
   272→        issue.setdefault("detector", "unknown")
   273→        issue.setdefault("file", "")
   274→        issue.setdefault("tier", 3)
   275→        issue.setdefault("confidence", "low")
   276→        issue.setdefault("summary", "")

   291→        issue.setdefault("suppressed_at", None)
   292→        issue.setdefault("suppression_pattern", None)
   293→
   294→    for issue_id in to_remove:

   308→def validate_state_invariants(state: StateModel) -> None:
   309→    """Raise ValueError when core state invariants are violated."""
   310→    if not isinstance(state.get("issues"), dict):
   311→        raise ValueError("state.issues must be a dict")
   312→    if not isinstance(state.get("stats"), dict):
   313→        raise ValueError("state.stats must be a dict")
   314→
   315→    all_issues = state["issues"]
   316→    for issue_id, issue in all_issues.items():
   317→        if not isinstance(issue, dict):
   318→            raise ValueError(f"issue {issue_id!r} must be a dict")
   319→        if issue.get("id") != issue_id:
   320→            raise ValueError(f"issue id mismatch for {issue_id!r}")
   321→        if issue.get("status") not in _ALLOWED_ISSUE_STATUSES:
   322→            raise ValueError(
   323→                f"issue {issue_id!r} has invalid status {issue.get('status')!r}"

   325→
   326→        tier = issue.get("tier")
   327→        if not isinstance(tier, int) or tier < 1 or tier > 4:
   328→            raise ValueError(f"issue {issue_id!r} has invalid tier {tier!r}")
   329→
   330→        reopen_count = issue.get("reopen_count")
   331→        if not isinstance(reopen_count, int) or reopen_count < 0:
   332→            raise ValueError(

    57→

    65→
    66→    name: str

1→"""Shared display utilities for command output."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→
     6→def short_issue_id(fid: str) -> str:
     7→    """Extract the 8-char hash suffix from a issue ID for compact display.
     8→
     9→    Issue IDs look like ``review::.::holistic::dim::identifier::abcdef12``.
    10→    Commands accept the hash suffix as a shorthand for the full ID.
    11→    """
    12→    if "::" in fid:
    13→        suffix = fid.rsplit("::", 1)[-1]
    14→        if len(suffix) >= 8:
    15→            return suffix[:8]
    16→    return fid
    17→
    18→
    19→__all__ = ["short_issue_id"]
    20→

    17→
    18→@dataclass
    19→class TriageGuardrailResult:
    20→    """Structured result from triage staleness detection."""
    21→
    22→    is_stale: bool = False

    26→
    27→def triage_guardrail_status(
    28→    *,
    29→    plan: dict | None = None,
    30→    state: dict | None = None,
    31→) -> TriageGuardrailResult:
    32→    """Pure detection: is triage stale? Returns structured result, no side effects."""
    33→    try:
    34→        resolved_plan = plan if isinstance(plan, dict) else load_plan()
    35→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
    36→        return TriageGuardrailResult()
    37→
    38→    resolved_state = state or {}

    40→    if not is_triage_stale(resolved_plan, resolved_state):
    41→        return TriageGuardrailResult(_plan=resolved_plan)
    42→
    43→    new_ids: set[str] = set()
    44→    if resolved_state:
    45→        new_ids = compute_new_issue_ids(resolved_plan, resolved_state)
    46→
    47→    return TriageGuardrailResult(is_stale=True, new_ids=new_ids, _plan=resolved_plan)
    48→
    49→
    50→def print_triage_guardrail_info(
    51→    *,
    52→    plan: dict | None = None,
    53→    state: dict | None = None,
    54→) -> bool:
    55→    """Print yellow info banner if triage is stale. Returns True if banner was shown."""
    56→    result = triage_guardrail_status(plan=plan, state=state)
    57→    if not result.is_stale:
    58→        return False
    59→
    60→    if result.new_ids:
    61→        print(colorize(
    62→            f"  {len(result.new_ids)} new review issue(s) not yet triaged.",
    63→            "yellow",
    64→        ))
    65→
    66→    if result._plan is not None:
    67→        banner = triage_phase_banner(result._plan)
    68→        if banner:
    69→            print(colorize(f"  {banner}", "yellow"))
    70→
    71→    return True
    72→

    74→def require_triage_current_or_exit(
    75→    *,
    76→    state: dict,
    77→    bypass: bool = False,
    78→    attest: str = "",
    79→) -> None:
    80→    """Gate: exit(1) if triage is stale and not bypassed. Name signals the exit."""
    81→    result = triage_guardrail_status(state=state)
    82→    if not result.is_stale:
    83→        return
    84→
    85→    if bypass and attest and len(attest.strip()) >= 30:

    92→    new_ids = result.new_ids
    93→    lines = [
    94→        f"BLOCKED: {len(new_ids) or 'some'} new review issue(s) have not been triaged."
    95→    ]
    96→    if new_ids:
    97→        for fid in sorted(new_ids)[:5]:
    98→            f = state.get("issues", {}).get(fid, {})
    99→            lines.append(f"    * [{short_issue_id(fid)}] {f.get('summary', '')}")
   100→        if len(new_ids) > 5:
   101→            lines.append(f"    ... and {len(new_ids) - 5} more")
   102→    lines.append("")

   104→    lines.append("  (Review new issues, then either --confirm-existing or re-plan.)")
   105→    lines.append("")
   106→    lines.append("  View new items:  desloppify plan queue --sort recent")
   107→    lines.append('  To bypass: --force-resolve --attest "I understand the plan may be stale..."')
   108→    raise CommandError("\n".join(lines))

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import logging
     6→from collections.abc import Callable
     7→from functools import lru_cache

    11→from desloppify import languages as lang_api
    12→from desloppify.base.text.text_api import get_project_root
    13→
    14→if TYPE_CHECKING:

    18→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

    20→
    21→class LangResolutionError(SystemExit):
    22→    """Raised when language resolution fails with a user-facing message.
    23→
    24→    Inherits from SystemExit so that callers which don't catch it explicitly
    25→    will still terminate with a non-zero exit code, matching the previous
    26→    sys.exit(1) behaviour.  The CLI top-level catches it to print a clean
    27→    error without a traceback.
    28→    """
    29→
    30→    def __init__(self, message: str) -> None:
    31→        self.message = message
    32→        super().__init__(1)
    33→
    34→
    35→EXTRA_ROOT_MARKERS = (
    36→    "package.json",
    37→    "pyproject.toml",
    38→    "setup.py",
    39→    "setup.cfg",
    40→    "go.mod",
    41→    "Cargo.toml",
    42→)
    43→
    44→
    45→def _cache_once(fn: Callable[[], tuple[str, ...]]) -> Callable[[], tuple[str, ...]]:
    46→    """Cache a zero-arg function once while preserving cache_clear for tests."""
    47→    cached = lru_cache(maxsize=1)(fn)
    48→    return cached
    49→
    50→
    51→@_cache_once
    52→def _lang_config_markers() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    53→    """Collect project-root marker files from language plugins + fallback markers."""
    54→    markers = set(EXTRA_ROOT_MARKERS)
    55→
    56→    for lang_name in lang_api.available_langs():
    57→        try:
    58→            cfg = lang_api.get_lang(lang_name)
    59→        except (ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
    60→            logger.debug(
    61→                "Skipping language marker collection for %s: %s", lang_name, exc
    62→            )
    63→            continue
    64→        for marker in getattr(cfg, "detect_markers", []) or []:
    65→            if not isinstance(marker, str):
    66→                continue
    67→            cleaned = marker.strip()
    68→            if cleaned:
    69→                markers.add(cleaned)
    70→    return tuple(sorted(markers))
    71→
    72→
    73→def resolve_detection_root(
    74→    args,
    75→    *,
    76→    project_root: Path | None = None,
    77→    marker_provider: Callable[[], tuple[str, ...]] | None = None,
    78→) -> Path:
    79→    """Best root to auto-detect language from."""
    80→    marker_provider = marker_provider or _lang_config_markers
    81→    markers = marker_provider()
    82→    root = project_root if project_root is not None else get_project_root()
    83→
    84→    raw_path = getattr(args, "path", None)
    85→    if not raw_path:
    86→        return root
    87→
    88→    candidate = Path(raw_path)
    89→    if not candidate.is_absolute():
    90→        candidate = root / candidate
    91→    candidate = candidate.resolve()
    92→    search_root = candidate if candidate.is_dir() else candidate.parent
    93→
    94→    for root in (search_root, *search_root.parents):
    95→        if any((root / marker).exists() for marker in markers):
    96→            return root
    97→    return search_root
    98→
    99→
   100→def auto_detect_lang_name(args) -> str | None:
   101→    """Auto-detect language using the most relevant root for this command."""
   102→    root = resolve_detection_root(args)
   103→    detected = lang_api.auto_detect_lang(root)
   104→    if detected is None and root != get_project_root():
   105→        detected = lang_api.auto_detect_lang(get_project_root())
   106→    return detected
   107→
   108→
   109→def resolve_lang(args) -> LangConfig | None:
   110→    """Resolve language config from args, with auto-detection fallback."""
   111→    lang_name = getattr(args, "lang", None)
   112→    if lang_name is None:
   113→        lang_name = auto_detect_lang_name(args)
   114→    if lang_name is None:
   115→        return None
   116→    try:
   117→        return lang_api.get_lang(lang_name)
   118→    except ValueError as exc:
   119→        langs = lang_api.available_langs()
   120→        langs_str = ", ".join(langs) if langs else "registered language plugins"
   121→        raise LangResolutionError(
   122→            f"{exc}\n  Hint: use --lang to select manually (available: {langs_str})"
   123→        ) from exc
   124→
   125→
   126→def resolve_lang_settings(config: dict, lang: LangConfig) -> dict[str, object]:
   127→    """Resolve persisted per-language settings from config.languages.<lang>."""
   128→    if not isinstance(config, dict):
   129→        return lang.normalize_settings({})
   130→    languages = config.get("languages", {})
   131→    if not isinstance(languages, dict):
   132→        return lang.normalize_settings({})
   133→    raw = languages.get(lang.name, {})
   134→    return lang.normalize_settings(raw if isinstance(raw, dict) else {})
   135→

    33→                file=sys.stderr,
    34→            )
    35→        return result

    51→@dataclass(frozen=True)

    93→def build_work_queue(
    94→    state: StateModel,
    95→    *,
    96→    options: QueueBuildOptions | None = None,
    97→) -> WorkQueueResult:
    98→    """Build a ranked work queue from state issues.
    99→
   100→    Pipeline:
   101→    1. Gather — issue items, subjective dimensions, workflow stages
   102→    2. Score  — estimate impact from dimension headroom, apply floor
   103→    3. Order  — stamp plan positions, sort, filter to cluster focus
   104→    4. Limit  — truncate to count, optionally add explain metadata
   105→    """
   106→    opts = options or QueueBuildOptions()
   107→    plan, scan_path, status, threshold = _resolve_inputs(opts, state)
   108→
   109→    # 1. Gather
   110→    items = build_issue_items(
   111→        state, scan_path=scan_path, status_filter=status,
   112→        scope=opts.scope, chronic=opts.chronic,
   113→    )
   114→    items += _gather_subjective_items(state, opts, plan, threshold)
   115→    items += _gather_workflow_items(state, plan, status)

   119→    items = [i for i in items if _passes_impact_floor(i)]
   120→

   122→    new_ids, skipped = _plan_presort(items, state, plan)
   123→    items.sort(key=item_sort_key)

   127→    if not items:
   128→        items += _empty_queue_fallback(plan)

   138→        "total": total,

   144→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

   148→
   149→def _resolve_inputs(
   150→    opts: QueueBuildOptions, state: StateModel,
   151→) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None, str, float]:
   152→    """Resolve plan, scan_path, status, and subjective threshold from options."""
   153→    ctx = opts.context
   154→    plan = ctx.plan if ctx is not None else opts.plan
   155→
   156→    scan_path: str | None = (
   157→        state.get("scan_path")

   159→        else opts.scan_path  # type: ignore[assignment]
   160→    )

   166→    try:

   168→    except (TypeError, ValueError):

   170→    threshold = max(0.0, min(100.0, threshold))
   171→
   172→    return plan, scan_path, status, threshold

   184→    if opts.status not in {"open", "all"}:

   186→    if opts.chronic:

   189→    ctx = opts.context
   190→    policy = (
   191→        (ctx.policy if ctx is not None else None)
   192→        or opts.policy
   193→        or compute_subjective_visibility(state, plan=plan)

   196→    candidates = build_subjective_items(

   244→def _passes_impact_floor(item: dict) -> bool:
   245→    """Return True if item should survive the impact floor filter."""
   246→    if item.get("kind") != "issue":
   247→        return True
   248→    if item.get("is_review") or item.get("is_subjective"):
   249→        return True
   250→    impact = item.get("estimated_impact")
   251→    return not impact or impact >= _MIN_STANDALONE_IMPACT
   252→

   254→def _plan_presort(
   255→    items: list[dict], state: StateModel, plan: dict | None,
   256→) -> tuple[set[str], list[dict]]:
   257→    """Enrich plan metadata and stamp sort keys before sorting.
   258→
   259→    Returns ``(new_ids, skipped)`` — skipped items are removed from

   261→    """
   262→    if not plan:
   263→        return set(), []
   264→

   266→    enrich_plan_metadata(items, plan)
   267→    stamp_plan_sort_keys(items, plan, new_ids)
   268→    remaining, skipped = separate_skipped(items, plan)
   269→    items[:] = remaining
   270→    return new_ids, skipped
   271→
   272→
   273→def _plan_postsort(
   274→    items: list[dict],
   275→    skipped: list[dict],
   276→    plan: dict | None,
   277→    opts: QueueBuildOptions,

   286→    focused = filter_cluster_focus(items, plan, opts.cluster)
   287→    items[:] = focused

   292→    if not plan:
   293→        return []
   294→    plan_scores = plan.get("plan_start_scores", {})
   295→    if plan_scores.get("strict") is None:
   296→        return []
   297→    return [{
   298→        "id": "workflow::run-scan",
   299→        "kind": "workflow_action",
   300→        "summary": "Queue cleared \u2014 run scan to finalize and reveal your updated score.",
   301→        "primary_command": "desloppify scan",
   302→        "file": "",
   303→        "detector": "workflow",

    40→def enrich_with_impact(
    41→    items: list[dict[str, Any]], dimension_scores: dict[str, Any]
    42→) -> None:
    43→    """Stamp ``estimated_impact`` on each item based on dimension-level headroom.
    44→
    45→    Impact = ``overall_per_point * headroom`` where headroom = ``100 - score``.
    46→    Items in dimensions with more score headroom sort first.
    47→    """
    48→    if not dimension_scores:
    49→        for item in items:
    50→            item["estimated_impact"] = 0.0
    51→        return
    52→
    53→    breakdown = compute_health_breakdown(dimension_scores)
    54→    entries = breakdown.get("entries", [])
    55→
    56→    # Build lookup: normalized dimension name -> {per_point, headroom}
    57→    dim_impact: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
    58→    for entry in entries:
    59→        name = str(entry.get("name", "")).strip()
    60→        if not name:
    61→            continue
    62→        per_point = float(entry.get("overall_per_point", 0.0))
    63→        score = float(entry.get("score", 0.0))
    64→        headroom = 100.0 - score
    65→        dim_impact[name.lower()] = {"per_point": per_point, "headroom": headroom}
    66→
    67→    for item in items:
    68→        impact = _compute_item_impact(item, dim_impact, get_dimension_for_detector)
    69→        item["estimated_impact"] = impact
    70→
    71→
    72→def _compute_item_impact(
    73→    item: dict[str, Any],
    74→    dim_impact: dict[str, dict[str, float]],
    75→    get_dimension_for_detector,
    76→) -> float:
    77→    """Compute impact value for a single queue item."""
    78→    kind = item.get("kind", "issue")
    79→
    80→    # Subjective items (synthetic dimensions or subjective issues):
    81→    # look up by detail.dimension_name
    82→    if kind == "subjective_dimension" or item.get("is_subjective"):
    83→        dim_name = detail_dict(item).get("dimension_name", "")
    84→        entry = dim_impact.get(dim_name.lower())
    85→        if entry:
    86→            return entry["per_point"] * entry["headroom"]
    87→        return 0.0
    88→
    89→    # Mechanical issues: use detector -> dimension mapping
    90→    detector = item.get("detector", "")
    91→    if detector:
    92→        dimension = get_dimension_for_detector(detector)
    93→        if dimension:
    94→            entry = dim_impact.get(dimension.name.lower())
    95→            if entry:
    96→                return entry["per_point"] * entry["headroom"]
    97→
    98→    return 0.0
    99→

   102→    if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension":
   103→        detail = detail_dict(item)
   104→        return float(detail.get("strict_score", item.get("subjective_score", 100.0)))
   105→    return float(item.get("subjective_score", 100.0))

   108→def build_issue_items(
   109→    state: StateModel,
   110→    *,
   111→    scan_path: str | None,
   112→    status_filter: str,
   113→    scope: str | None,
   114→    chronic: bool,
   115→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   116→    scoped = path_scoped_issues(state.get("issues", {}), scan_path)
   117→    subjective_scores = subjective_strict_scores(state)
   118→    out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   119→
   120→    for issue_id, issue in scoped.items():
   121→        if issue.get("suppressed"):
   122→            continue
   123→        if not status_matches(issue.get("status", "open"), status_filter):
   124→            continue
   125→        if chronic and not (
   126→            issue.get("status") == "open" and issue.get("reopen_count", 0) >= 2
   127→        ):
   128→            continue
   129→
   130→        # Evidence-only: skip issues below standalone confidence threshold
   131→        detector = issue.get("detector", "")
   132→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   133→        if meta and meta.standalone_threshold:
   134→            threshold_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(meta.standalone_threshold, 9)
   135→            issue_rank = CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(issue.get("confidence", "low"), 9)
   136→            if issue_rank > threshold_rank:
   137→                continue
   138→
   139→        item = dict(issue)
   140→        item["id"] = issue_id
   141→        item["kind"] = "issue"
   142→        item["is_review"] = is_review_issue(item)
   143→        item["is_subjective"] = is_subjective_issue(item)
   144→        item["review_weight"] = (
   145→            review_issue_weight(item) if item["is_review"] else None
   146→        )
   147→        subjective_score = None
   148→        if item["is_subjective"]:
   149→            detail = detail_dict(issue)
   150→            dim_name = detail.get("dimension_name", "")
   151→            dim_key = detail.get("dimension", "") or slugify(dim_name)
   152→            subjective_score = subjective_scores.get(
   153→                dim_key, subjective_scores.get(dim_name.lower(), 100.0)
   154→            )
   155→        item["subjective_score"] = subjective_score
   156→        supported_fixers = supported_fixers_for_item(state, item)
   157→        item["primary_command"] = primary_command_for_issue(
   158→            item,
   159→            supported_fixers=supported_fixers,
   160→        )
   161→
   162→        if not scope_matches(item, scope):
   163→            continue
   164→        out.append(item)
   165→
   166→    return out
