   168→
   169→def _natural_sort_key(item: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple:
   170→    """Compute natural (non-plan-aware) ranking for queue items."""
   171→    kind = item.get("kind", "issue")
   172→
   173→    # Initial-review subjective items: highest priority
   174→    if kind == "subjective_dimension" and item.get("initial_review"):
   175→        return (_RANK_INITIAL_REVIEW, 0, subjective_score_value(item), item.get("id", ""))
   176→
   177→    # Triage stage items: stage order, blocked after unblocked
   178→    if kind == "workflow_stage":
   179→        blocked_penalty = 1 if item.get("is_blocked") else 0
   180→        stage_index = int(item.get("stage_index", 0))
   181→        return (_RANK_TRIAGE_STAGE, blocked_penalty, stage_index, item.get("id", ""))
   182→
   183→    # Workflow action items (e.g. create-plan)
   184→    if kind == "workflow_action":
   185→        return (_RANK_WORKFLOW, 0, 0, item.get("id", ""))
   186→
   187→    if kind == "cluster":
   188→        # Clusters sort before individual issues, ordered by action type
   189→        action_pri = ACTION_TYPE_PRIORITY.get(
   190→            item.get("action_type", "manual_fix"), 3
   191→        )
   192→        return (
   193→            _RANK_CLUSTER,
   194→            action_pri,
   195→            -int(item.get("member_count", 0)),
   196→            item.get("id", ""),
   197→        )
   198→
   199→    impact = item.get("estimated_impact", 0.0)
   200→
   201→    if kind == "subjective_dimension" or item.get("is_subjective"):
   202→        return (
   203→            _RANK_ISSUE,
   204→            -impact,
   205→            subjective_score_value(item),
   206→            item.get("id", ""),
   207→        )
   208→
   209→    detail = detail_dict(item)
   210→    review_weight = float(item.get("review_weight", 0.0) or 0.0)
   211→    return (
   212→        _RANK_ISSUE,
   213→        -impact,
   214→        CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(item.get("confidence", "low"), 9),
   215→        -review_weight,
   216→        -int(detail.get("count", 0) or 0),
   217→        item.get("id", ""),
   218→    )
   219→
   220→
   221→def item_sort_key(item: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple:
   222→    """Unified sort key: plan position first, then natural ranking.
   223→
   224→    When ``_plan_position`` is stamped (by :func:`stamp_plan_sort_keys`),
   225→    planned items sort first in plan order, then existing items by natural
   226→    ranking, then newly-discovered items by natural ranking.
   227→
   228→    When no plan fields are stamped, falls back to pure natural ranking.
   229→    """
   230→    plan_pos = item.get("_plan_position")
   231→
   232→    if plan_pos is not None:
   233→        kind = item.get("kind", "issue")
   234→        # Triage stages: even when explicitly planned, maintain the
   235→        # blocked-before-unblocked invariant for correctness.
   236→        if kind == "workflow_stage":
   237→            blocked = 1 if item.get("is_blocked") else 0
   238→            stage_idx = int(item.get("stage_index", 0))
   239→            return (_TIER_PLANNED, blocked, stage_idx, item.get("id", ""))
   240→        return (_TIER_PLANNED, 0, plan_pos, item.get("id", ""))
   241→
   242→    is_new = item.get("_is_new", False)
   243→    group = _TIER_NEW if is_new else _TIER_EXISTING
   244→    return (group, *_natural_sort_key(item))
   245→
   246→
   247→def item_explain(item: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   248→    kind = item.get("kind", "issue")
   249→    if kind == "workflow_stage":
   250→        return {
   251→            "kind": "workflow_stage",

   253→            "is_blocked": item.get("is_blocked", False),
   254→            "blocked_by": item.get("blocked_by", []),
   255→            "policy": "Triage stages sort by dependency order; blocked stages follow unblocked.",
   256→            "ranking_factors": ["blocked_penalty asc", "stage_index asc"],
   257→        }
   258→
   259→    if kind == "workflow_action":
   260→        return {
   261→            "kind": "workflow_action",
   262→            "policy": "Workflow items sort after triage stages, before issues.",
   263→            "ranking_factors": ["id asc"],
   264→        }
   265→
   266→    if kind == "cluster":
   267→        return {
   268→            "kind": "cluster",
   269→            "estimated_impact": item.get("estimated_impact", 0.0),
   270→            "action_type": item.get("action_type", "manual_fix"),
   271→            "member_count": item.get("member_count", 0),
   272→            "policy": "Clusters sort before individual issues, ordered by action type then size.",
   273→            "ranking_factors": ["action_type asc", "member_count desc", "id asc"],
   274→        }
   275→
   276→    if kind == "subjective_dimension":
   277→        initial = item.get("initial_review", False)
   278→        return {
   279→            "kind": "subjective_dimension",
   280→            "estimated_impact": item.get("estimated_impact", 0.0),
   281→            "subjective_score": subjective_score_value(item),
   282→            "initial_review": initial,
   283→            "policy": (
   284→                "Initial review items sort first (onboarding priority)."
   285→                if initial else
   286→                "Sorted by dimension impact (score headroom × weight), then subjective score."
   287→            ),
   288→            "ranking_factors": ["estimated_impact desc", "subjective_score asc", "id asc"],
   289→        }
   290→
   291→    detail = detail_dict(item)
   292→    confidence = item.get("confidence", "low")
   293→    is_subjective = bool(item.get("is_subjective"))
   294→    is_review = bool(item.get("is_review"))
   295→    ranking_factors: list[str]
   296→    if is_subjective:
   297→        ranking_factors = ["estimated_impact desc", "subjective_score asc", "id asc"]
   298→    elif is_review:
   299→        ranking_factors = [
   300→            "estimated_impact desc",
   301→            "confidence asc",
   302→            "review_weight desc",
   303→            "count desc",
   304→            "id asc",
   305→        ]
   306→    else:
   307→        ranking_factors = ["estimated_impact desc", "confidence asc", "count desc", "id asc"]
   308→    explain = {
   309→        "kind": "issue",
   310→        "estimated_impact": item.get("estimated_impact", 0.0),
   311→        "confidence": confidence,
   312→        "confidence_rank": CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(confidence, 9),
   313→        "count": int(detail.get("count", 0) or 0),
   314→        "id": item.get("id", ""),
   315→        "ranking_factors": ranking_factors,
   316→    }
   317→    if is_review:
   318→        explain["review_weight"] = float(item.get("review_weight", 0.0) or 0.0)
   319→    if is_subjective:
   320→        explain["policy"] = (
   321→            "Sorted by dimension impact (score headroom × weight), then subjective score."
   322→        )
   323→        explain["subjective_score"] = subjective_score_value(item)
   324→    return explain
   325→
   326→
   327→def group_queue_items(
   328→    items: list[dict[str, Any]], group: str
   329→) -> dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
   330→    """Group queue items for alternate output modes."""
   331→    grouped: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
   332→    for item in items:
   333→        if group == "file":
   334→            key = item.get("file", "")
   335→        elif group == "detector":
   336→            key = item.get("detector", "")
   337→        elif group == "cluster":
   338→            plan_cluster = item.get("plan_cluster")
   339→            key = plan_cluster["name"] if isinstance(plan_cluster, dict) else "(unclustered)"
   340→        else:
   341→            key = "items"
   342→        grouped.setdefault(key, []).append(item)
   343→    return grouped
   344→
   345→

1→"""Health score aggregation helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.base.text.text_api import is_numeric
     6→from desloppify.engine._scoring.policy.core import (
     7→    MECHANICAL_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS,
     8→    MECHANICAL_WEIGHT_FRACTION,
     9→    MIN_SAMPLE,
    10→    SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS,
    11→    SUBJECTIVE_WEIGHT_FRACTION,
    12→)
    13→
    14→
    15→def _normalize_dimension_name(name: str) -> str:
    16→    return " ".join(str(name).strip().lower().split())
    17→
    18→
    19→def _mechanical_dimension_weight(name: str) -> float:
    20→    return float(
    21→        MECHANICAL_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS.get(
    22→            _normalize_dimension_name(name),
    23→            1.0,
    24→        )
    25→    )
    26→
    27→
    28→def _subjective_dimension_weight(name: str, data: dict) -> float:
    29→    subjective_meta = (
    30→        data.get("detectors", {}).get("subjective_assessment", {})
    31→        if isinstance(data, dict)
    32→        else {}
    33→    )
    34→    configured = (
    35→        subjective_meta.get("configured_weight")
    36→        if isinstance(subjective_meta, dict)
    37→        else None
    38→    )
    39→    if is_numeric(configured):
    40→        return max(0.0, float(configured))
    41→
    42→    return float(
    43→        SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSION_WEIGHTS.get(
    44→            _normalize_dimension_name(name),
    45→            1.0,
    46→        )
    47→    )
    48→
    49→
    50→def compute_health_breakdown(
    51→    dimension_scores: dict,
    52→    *,
    53→    score_key: str = "score",
    54→) -> dict[str, object]:
    55→    """Return pool averages and weighted contribution breakdown for score transparency."""
    56→    if not dimension_scores:
    57→        return {
    58→            "overall_score": 100.0,
    59→            "mechanical_fraction": 1.0,
    60→            "subjective_fraction": 0.0,
    61→            "mechanical_avg": 100.0,
    62→            "subjective_avg": None,
    63→            "entries": [],
    64→        }
    65→
    66→    mech_sum = 0.0
    67→    mech_weight = 0.0
    68→    subj_sum = 0.0
    69→    subj_weight = 0.0
    70→    mechanical_rows: list[dict[str, float | str]] = []
    71→    subjective_rows: list[dict[str, float | str]] = []
    72→
    73→    for name, data in dimension_scores.items():
    74→        score = float(data.get(score_key, data.get("score", 0.0)))
    75→        is_subjective = "subjective_assessment" in data.get("detectors", {})
    76→        if is_subjective:
    77→            configured = max(0.0, _subjective_dimension_weight(name, data))
    78→            effective = configured
    79→            subj_sum += score * effective
    80→            subj_weight += effective
    81→            subjective_rows.append(
    82→                {
    83→                    "name": str(name),
    84→                    "score": score,
    85→                    "configured_weight": configured,
    86→                    "effective_weight": effective,
    87→                }
    88→            )
    89→            continue
    90→
    91→        checks = float(data.get("checks", 0) or 0)
    92→        sample_factor = min(1.0, checks / MIN_SAMPLE) if checks > 0 else 0.0
    93→        configured = max(0.0, _mechanical_dimension_weight(name))
    94→        effective = configured * sample_factor
    95→        mech_sum += score * effective
    96→        mech_weight += effective
    97→        mechanical_rows.append(
    98→            {
    99→                "name": str(name),
   100→                "score": score,
   101→                "checks": checks,
   102→                "sample_factor": sample_factor,
   103→                "configured_weight": configured,
   104→                "effective_weight": effective,
   105→            }
   106→        )
   107→
   108→    mech_avg = (mech_sum / mech_weight) if mech_weight > 0 else 100.0
   109→    subj_avg = (subj_sum / subj_weight) if subj_weight > 0 else None
   110→
   111→    if subj_avg is None:
   112→        mechanical_fraction = 1.0
   113→        subjective_fraction = 0.0
   114→        overall_score = round(mech_avg, 1)
   115→    elif mech_weight == 0:
   116→        mechanical_fraction = 0.0
   117→        subjective_fraction = 1.0
   118→        overall_score = round(subj_avg, 1)
   119→    else:
   120→        mechanical_fraction = MECHANICAL_WEIGHT_FRACTION
   121→        subjective_fraction = SUBJECTIVE_WEIGHT_FRACTION
   122→        overall_score = round(
   123→            mech_avg * mechanical_fraction + subj_avg * subjective_fraction,
   124→            1,
   125→        )
   126→
   127→    entries: list[dict[str, float | str]] = []
   128→    for row in mechanical_rows:
   129→        pool_share = (
   130→            float(row["effective_weight"]) / mech_weight if mech_weight > 0 else 0.0
   131→        )
   132→        per_point = mechanical_fraction * pool_share
   133→        score = float(row["score"])
   134→        entries.append(
   135→            {
   136→                "name": str(row["name"]),
   137→                "pool": "mechanical",
   138→                "score": score,
   139→                "checks": float(row["checks"]),
   140→                "sample_factor": float(row["sample_factor"]),
   141→                "configured_weight": float(row["configured_weight"]),
   142→                "effective_weight": float(row["effective_weight"]),
   143→                "pool_share": pool_share,
   144→                "overall_per_point": per_point,
   145→                "overall_contribution": per_point * score,
   146→                "overall_drag": per_point * (100.0 - score),
   147→            }
   148→        )
   149→
   150→    for row in subjective_rows:
   151→        pool_share = (
   152→            float(row["effective_weight"]) / subj_weight if subj_weight > 0 else 0.0
   153→        )
   154→        per_point = subjective_fraction * pool_share
   155→        score = float(row["score"])
   156→        entries.append(
   157→            {
   158→                "name": str(row["name"]),
   159→                "pool": "subjective",
   160→                "score": score,
   161→                "checks": 0.0,
   162→                "sample_factor": 1.0,
   163→                "configured_weight": float(row["configured_weight"]),
   164→                "effective_weight": float(row["effective_weight"]),
   165→                "pool_share": pool_share,
   166→                "overall_per_point": per_point,
   167→                "overall_contribution": per_point * score,
   168→                "overall_drag": per_point * (100.0 - score),
   169→            }
   170→        )
   171→
   172→    return {
   173→        "overall_score": overall_score,
   174→        "mechanical_fraction": mechanical_fraction,
   175→        "subjective_fraction": subjective_fraction,
   176→        "mechanical_avg": mech_avg,
   177→        "subjective_avg": subj_avg,
   178→        "entries": entries,
   179→    }
   180→
   181→
   182→def compute_health_score(
   183→    dimension_scores: dict,
   184→    *,
   185→    score_key: str = "score",
   186→) -> float:
   187→    """Budget-weighted blend of mechanical and subjective dimension scores."""
   188→    return float(
   189→        compute_health_breakdown(dimension_scores, score_key=score_key)[
   190→            "overall_score"
   191→        ]
   192→    )
   193→
   194→
   195→__all__ = ["compute_health_breakdown", "compute_health_score"]
   196→
   197→

1→"""Orphaned file detection: files with zero importers that aren't entry points."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from collections.abc import Callable
     6→from dataclasses import dataclass
     7→from pathlib import Path
     8→
     9→from desloppify.base.discovery.api import rel
    10→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import count_lines
    11→
    12→
    13→@dataclass
    14→class OrphanedDetectionOptions:
    15→    """Optional behavior flags for orphaned-file detection."""
    16→
    17→    extra_entry_patterns: list[str] | None = None
    18→    extra_barrel_names: set[str] | None = None
    19→    dynamic_import_finder: Callable[[Path, list[str]], set[str]] | None = None
    20→    alias_resolver: Callable[[str], str] | None = None
    21→
    22→
    23→def _is_dynamically_imported(
    24→    filepath: str,
    25→    dynamic_targets: set[str],
    26→    alias_resolver: Callable[[str], str] | None = None,
    27→) -> bool:
    28→    """Check if a file is referenced by any dynamic/side-effect import."""
    29→    r = rel(filepath)
    30→    stem = Path(filepath).stem
    31→    name_no_ext = str(Path(r).with_suffix(""))
    32→
    33→    for target in dynamic_targets:
    34→        resolved = alias_resolver(target) if alias_resolver else target
    35→        resolved = resolved.lstrip("./")
    36→        if resolved == name_no_ext or resolved == r:
    37→            return True
    38→        if name_no_ext.endswith("/" + resolved) or name_no_ext.endswith(resolved):
    39→            return True
    40→        if resolved.endswith("/" + stem) or resolved == stem:
    41→            return True
    42→        if resolved.endswith("/" + Path(filepath).name):
    43→            return True
    44→
    45→    return False
    46→
    47→
    48→def detect_orphaned_files(
    49→    path: Path,
    50→    graph: dict,
    51→    extensions: list[str],
    52→    options: OrphanedDetectionOptions | None = None,
    53→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    54→    """Find files with zero importers that aren't known entry points."""
    55→    resolved_options = options or OrphanedDetectionOptions()
    56→    all_entry_patterns = resolved_options.extra_entry_patterns or []
    57→    all_barrel_names = resolved_options.extra_barrel_names or set()
    58→    dynamic_import_finder = resolved_options.dynamic_import_finder
    59→    alias_resolver = resolved_options.alias_resolver
    60→
    61→    dynamic_targets = (
    62→        dynamic_import_finder(path, extensions) if dynamic_import_finder else set()
    63→    )
    64→
    65→    total_files = len(graph)
    66→    entries = []
    67→    for filepath, entry in graph.items():
    68→        if entry["importer_count"] > 0:
    69→            continue
    70→
    71→        r = rel(filepath)
    72→
    73→        if any(p in r for p in all_entry_patterns):
    74→            continue
    75→
    76→        basename = Path(filepath).name
    77→        if basename in all_barrel_names:
    78→            continue
    79→
    80→        if dynamic_targets and _is_dynamically_imported(
    81→            filepath, dynamic_targets, alias_resolver
    82→        ):
    83→            continue
    84→
    85→        try:
    86→            loc = count_lines(Path(filepath))
    87→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
    88→            loc = 0
    89→
    90→        if loc < 10:
    91→            continue
    92→
    93→        entries.append(
    94→            {
    95→                "file": filepath,
    96→                "loc": loc,
    97→                "import_count": entry.get("import_count", 0),
    98→            }
    99→        )
   100→
   101→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: -e["loc"]), total_files
   102→

1→"""Large file detection (LOC threshold)."""
     2→
     3→import logging
     4→from pathlib import Path
     5→
     6→from desloppify.base.output.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
     7→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import count_lines, resolve_scan_file
     8→
     9→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    10→
    11→
    12→def detect_large_files(
    13→    path: Path, file_finder, threshold: int = 500
    14→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    15→    """Find files exceeding a line count threshold."""
    16→    files = file_finder(path)
    17→    entries = []
    18→    for filepath in files:
    19→        try:
    20→            p = resolve_scan_file(filepath, scan_root=path)
    21→            loc = count_lines(p)
    22→            if loc > threshold:
    23→                entries.append({"file": filepath, "loc": loc})
    24→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
    25→            log_best_effort_failure(
    26→                logger,
    27→                f"read large-file detector candidate {filepath}",
    28→                exc,
    29→            )
    30→            continue
    31→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: -e["loc"]), len(files)
    32→

1→"""Naming consistency analysis: flag directories with mixed filename conventions."""
     2→
     3→from collections import defaultdict
     4→from pathlib import Path
     5→
     6→from desloppify.base.discovery.api import rel
     7→
     8→
     9→def _classify_convention(filename: str) -> str | None:
    10→    """Classify a filename (without extension) into a naming convention."""
    11→    stem = filename.rsplit(".", 1)[0] if "." in filename else filename
    12→    if not stem:
    13→        return None
    14→
    15→    if "-" in stem and stem == stem.lower():
    16→        return "kebab-case"
    17→    if stem[0].isupper() and "-" not in stem:
    18→        return "PascalCase"
    19→    if stem[0].islower() and any(c.isupper() for c in stem) and "-" not in stem:
    20→        return "camelCase"
    21→    if "_" in stem and stem == stem.lower():
    22→        return "snake_case"
    23→    if stem.islower() and "-" not in stem:
    24→        return "flat_lower"
    25→    return None
    26→
    27→
    28→def detect_naming_inconsistencies(
    29→    path: Path,
    30→    file_finder,
    31→    skip_names: set[str] | None = None,
    32→    skip_dirs: set[str] | None = None,
    33→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    34→    """Find directories where minority naming convention is significant.
    35→
    36→    Thresholds: minority must have >= 5 files (absolute) and >= 15% of total (proportional).
    37→    """
    38→    all_skip_names = skip_names or set()
    39→    all_skip_dirs = skip_dirs or set()
    40→    files = file_finder(path)
    41→
    42→    dir_files: dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
    43→
    44→    for filepath in files:
    45→        p = Path(filepath)
    46→        dirname = str(p.parent)
    47→        rdir = rel(dirname)
    48→        filename = p.name
    49→
    50→        if filename in all_skip_names:
    51→            continue
    52→        if rdir in all_skip_dirs:
    53→            continue
    54→
    55→        convention = _classify_convention(filename)
    56→        if convention:
    57→            dir_files[dirname][convention].append(filename)
    58→
    59→    entries = []
    60→    for dirname, conventions in dir_files.items():
    61→        if len(conventions) < 2:
    62→            continue
    63→
    64→        sorted_conventions = sorted(conventions.items(), key=lambda x: -len(x[1]))
    65→        majority_name, majority_files = sorted_conventions[0]
    66→        total = sum(len(fs) for fs in conventions.values())
    67→
    68→        for conv_name, conv_files in sorted_conventions[1:]:
    69→            if len(conv_files) < 5:
    70→                continue
    71→            if len(conv_files) / total < 0.15:
    72→                continue
    73→
    74→            entries.append(
    75→                {
    76→                    "directory": rel(dirname),
    77→                    "majority": majority_name,
    78→                    "majority_count": len(majority_files),
    79→                    "minority": conv_name,
    80→                    "minority_count": len(conv_files),
    81→                    "total_files": total,
    82→                    "outliers": sorted(conv_files[:10]),
    83→                }
    84→            )
    85→
    86→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: -e["minority_count"]), len(dir_files)
    87→

1→"""God class/component detection via configurable rule-based analysis."""
     2→
     3→
     4→def detect_gods(classes, rules, min_reasons: int = 2) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
     5→    """Find god classes/components — entities with too many responsibilities."""
     6→    entries = []
     7→    for cls in classes:
     8→        reasons = []
     9→        for rule in rules:
    10→            value = rule.extract(cls)
    11→            if value >= rule.threshold:
    12→                reasons.append(f"{value} {rule.description}")
    13→
    14→        if len(reasons) >= min_reasons:
    15→            entries.append(
    16→                {
    17→                    "file": cls.file,
    18→                    "name": cls.name,
    19→                    "loc": cls.loc,
    20→                    "reasons": reasons,
    21→                    "signal_text": f"{cls.name} ({', '.join(reasons[:2])})",
    22→                    "detail": {**cls.metrics, "name": cls.name},
    23→                }
    24→            )
    25→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: -e["loc"]), len(classes)
    26→

    44→
    45→        Use this instead of ``queue_total`` when gating on "is there work left?"
    46→        (e.g. scan preflight, plan-start-score clearing).  Workflow items like
    47→        ``workflow::run-scan`` guide the user but are not work to complete.
    48→        """
    49→        return max(0, self.queue_total - self.workflow)
    50→
    51→
    52→def plan_aware_queue_breakdown(
    53→    state: dict,
    54→    plan: dict | None = None,
    55→    *,
    56→    context: QueueContext | None = None,
    57→) -> QueueBreakdown:
    58→    """Build a full :class:`QueueBreakdown` from a single ``build_work_queue`` call.
    59→
    60→    When *context* is provided, its ``plan`` and ``policy`` are forwarded to
    61→    ``build_work_queue`` so the counts agree with the caller's resolution.
    62→    """
    63→    effective_plan = context.plan if context is not None else plan
    64→
    65→    result = work_queue_core_mod.build_work_queue(
    66→        state,
    67→        options=work_queue_core_mod.QueueBuildOptions(
    68→            status="open",
    69→            count=None,
    70→            plan=effective_plan if context is None else None,
    71→            include_skipped=False,
    72→            context=context,
    73→        ),
    74→    )
    75→
    76→    # Collapse clusters for display-level counting
    77→    items = result.get("items", [])
    78→    if effective_plan and not effective_plan.get("active_cluster"):
    79→        items = collapse_clusters(items, effective_plan)
    80→
    81→    queue_total = len(items)
    82→
    83→    # Count subjective and workflow items in the queue.
    84→    # Collapsed clusters whose members are all subjective count as subjective.
    85→    subjective = sum(
    86→        1 for item in items
    87→        if is_subjective_queue_item(item)
    88→    )
    89→    workflow = sum(
    90→        1 for item in items
    91→        if item.get("kind") in ("workflow_stage", "workflow_action")
    92→    )
    93→
    94→    # Plan-derived counts
    95→    plan_ordered = 0
    96→    skipped = 0
    97→    if effective_plan:
    98→        skipped = len(effective_plan.get("skipped", {}))
    99→        # plan_ordered = items that are in queue_order minus skipped
   100→        queue_order = effective_plan.get("queue_order", [])
   101→        skipped_ids = set(effective_plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   102→        plan_ordered = sum(1 for fid in queue_order if fid not in skipped_ids)
   103→
   104→    # Focus cluster info
   105→    focus_cluster = None
   106→    focus_cluster_count = 0
   107→    focus_cluster_total = 0
   108→    if effective_plan:
   109→        active = effective_plan.get("active_cluster")
   110→        if active:
   111→            focus_cluster = active
   112→            cluster_data = effective_plan.get("clusters", {}).get(active, {})
   113→            focus_cluster_total = len(cluster_data.get("issue_ids", []))
   114→            # Count how many cluster members are still in the queue
   115→            cluster_member_ids = set(cluster_data.get("issue_ids", []))
   116→            open_issues = {
   117→                fid
   118→                for fid, f in state.get("issues", {}).items()
   119→                if f.get("status") == "open"
   120→            }
   121→            focus_cluster_count = len(cluster_member_ids & open_issues)
   122→
   123→    return QueueBreakdown(
   124→        queue_total=queue_total,
   125→        plan_ordered=plan_ordered,
   126→        skipped=skipped,
   127→        subjective=subjective,
   128→        workflow=workflow,
   129→        focus_cluster=focus_cluster,
   130→        focus_cluster_count=focus_cluster_count,
   131→        focus_cluster_total=focus_cluster_total,
   132→    )
   133→
   134→
   135→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   136→# Formatting helpers — single source of truth for queue display
   137→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   138→
   139→def format_plan_delta(live: float, frozen: float) -> str:
   140→    """Format plan-start vs live delta, or '' if below threshold."""
   141→    if abs(live - frozen) < 0.05:
   142→        return ""
   143→    delta = round(live - frozen, 1)
   144→    return f"{'+' if delta > 0 else ''}{delta:.1f}"
   145→
   146→
   147→def format_queue_headline(breakdown: QueueBreakdown) -> str:
   148→    """The one-line Queue summary. Same format everywhere.
   149→
   150→    Examples::
   151→
   152→        Queue: 1934 items (292 planned · 23 skipped)
   153→        Queue: 1934 items
   154→    """
   155→    n = breakdown.queue_total
   156→    label = f"Queue: {n} item{'s' if n != 1 else ''}"
   157→
   158→    # Parenthesized segments
   159→    segments: list[str] = []
   160→    if breakdown.workflow > 0:
   161→        segments.append(f"{breakdown.workflow} planning step{'s' if breakdown.workflow != 1 else ''}")
   162→    if breakdown.plan_ordered > 0:
   163→        segments.append(f"{breakdown.plan_ordered} planned")
   164→    if breakdown.skipped > 0:
   165→        segments.append(f"{breakdown.skipped} skipped")
   166→    if breakdown.subjective > 0:
   167→        segments.append(f"{breakdown.subjective} subjective")
   168→    if segments:
   169→        sep = " \u00b7 "
   170→        detail = sep.join(segments)
   171→        return f"{label} ({detail})"
   172→    return label
   173→
   174→
   175→def format_queue_block(
   176→    breakdown: QueueBreakdown,
   177→    *,
   178→    frozen_score: float | None = None,
   179→    live_score: float | None = None,
   180→) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
   181→    """Full queue block: focus banner + queue line + contextual hints.
   182→
   183→    Returns a list of ``(text, style)`` pairs ready for ``colorize()``.
   184→    """
   185→    lines: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
   186→
   187→    # Focus banner (prominent, separate)
   188→    if breakdown.focus_cluster:
   189→        focus_line = (
   190→            f"  Focus: `{breakdown.focus_cluster}` "
   191→            f"\u2014 {breakdown.focus_cluster_count}/{breakdown.focus_cluster_total}"
   192→            f" items remaining"
   193→        )
   194→        lines.append((focus_line, "cyan"))
   195→
   196→    # Score line: show both frozen plan-start and live score when available
   197→    if frozen_score is not None:
   198→        delta_str = format_plan_delta(live_score, frozen_score) if live_score is not None else ""
   199→        if delta_str:
   200→            lines.append((
   201→                f"  Score: strict {live_score:.1f}/100 (plan start: {frozen_score:.1f}, {delta_str})",
   202→                "cyan",
   203→            ))
   204→        else:
   205→            lines.append((
   206→                f"  Score (frozen at plan start): strict {frozen_score:.1f}/100",
   207→                "cyan",
   208→            ))
   209→
   210→    # Queue headline — always the same
   211→    lines.append((f"  {format_queue_headline(breakdown)}", "bold"))
   212→
   213→    # Contextual hints (dim)
   214→    if breakdown.focus_cluster:
   215→        lines.append((
   216→            f"  Unfocus: `desloppify plan focus --clear`"
   217→            f" \u00b7 Cluster details: `desloppify next --cluster {breakdown.focus_cluster} --count 10`",
   218→            "dim",
   219→        ))
   220→    elif breakdown.plan_ordered > 0 or breakdown.skipped > 0:
   221→        lines.append((
   222→            "  Details: `desloppify plan queue`"
   223→            " \u00b7 Skip: `desloppify plan skip <id>`",
   224→            "dim",
   225→        ))
   226→    else:
   227→        lines.append((
   228→            "  Start planning: `desloppify plan`",
   229→            "dim",
   230→        ))
   231→
   232→    return lines
   233→
   234→
   235→def get_plan_start_strict(plan: dict | None) -> float | None:
   236→    """Extract the frozen plan-start strict score, or None if unset."""
   237→    if not plan:
   238→        return None
   239→    return plan.get("plan_start_scores", {}).get("strict")
   240→
   241→
   242→def print_frozen_score_with_queue_context(
   243→    plan: dict,
   244→    queue_remaining: int,
   245→    *,
   246→    breakdown: QueueBreakdown,
   247→    live_score: float | None = None,
   248→) -> None:
   249→    """Show frozen plan-start score + queue progress."""
   250→    scores = plan.get("plan_start_scores", {})
   251→    strict = scores.get("strict")
   252→    if strict is None:
   253→        return
   254→
   255→    block = format_queue_block(breakdown, frozen_score=strict, live_score=live_score)
   256→    print()
   257→    for text, style in block:
   258→        print(colorize(text, style))
   259→    if queue_remaining > 0:
   260→        print(colorize(
   261→            "  Score will not update until the queue is clear and you run `desloppify scan`.",
   262→            "dim",
   263→        ))
   264→
   265→
   266→def _print_objective_drained_banner(
   267→    frozen_strict: float,
   268→    remaining: int,
   269→    breakdown: QueueBreakdown,
   270→) -> None:
   271→    """Show a phase-transition banner when objective work is drained."""
   272→    kind_labels: list[str] = []
   273→    if breakdown.subjective > 0:
   274→        kind_labels.append("subjective")
   275→    if breakdown.workflow > 0:
   276→        kind_labels.append("workflow")
   277→    kind_desc = " + ".join(kind_labels) if kind_labels else "non-objective"
   278→    print(colorize(
   279→        f"\n  Objective queue complete (plan-start was {frozen_strict:.1f})."
   280→        f" {remaining} {kind_desc} item{'s' if remaining != 1 else ''} remain.",
   281→        "cyan",
   282→    ))
   283→    print(colorize(
   284→        "  Run `desloppify next` for remaining work,"
   285→        " then `desloppify scan` to finalize.",
   286→        "dim",
   287→    ))
   288→
   289→
   290→def print_execution_or_reveal(
   291→    state: dict,
   292→    prev,
   293→    plan: dict | None,
   294→) -> None:
   295→    """Context-aware score display: frozen plan-start score or live scores.
   296→
   297→    Three display modes:
   298→
   299→    1. **Frozen** — objective queue items remain → show frozen plan-start score.
   300→    2. **Phase transition** — objective drained, subjective/workflow remains
   301→       → show live scores + transition banner.
   302→    3. **Live** — no active plan cycle or queue is clear → show live scores.
   303→    """
   304→    frozen_strict: float | None = None
   305→    breakdown: QueueBreakdown | None = None
   306→
   307→    if plan and plan.get("plan_start_scores", {}).get("strict") is not None:
   308→        frozen_strict = plan["plan_start_scores"]["strict"]
   309→        try:
   310→            breakdown = plan_aware_queue_breakdown(state, plan)
   311→        except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   312→            _logger.debug("queue breakdown computation skipped", exc_info=True)
   313→
   314→    remaining = breakdown.queue_total if breakdown else 0
   315→
   316→    # Frozen: objective work remains — show frozen plan-start score and return
   317→    if remaining > 0 and frozen_strict is not None:
   318→        objective_remaining = remaining - breakdown.subjective - breakdown.workflow
   319→        if objective_remaining > 0:
   320→            # Compute live score for delta display alongside frozen
   321→            print_frozen_score_with_queue_context(
   322→                plan, remaining, breakdown=breakdown,
   323→                live_score=state_mod.score_snapshot(state).strict,
   324→            )
   325→            return
   326→
   327→    # Live scores (or phase transition): show current scores
   328→    score_update_mod = importlib.import_module(
   329→        "desloppify.app.commands.helpers.score_update"
   330→    )
   331→    score_update_mod.print_score_update(state, prev)
   332→
   333→    # Phase transition: objective drained but subjective/workflow remains
   334→    if remaining > 0 and frozen_strict is not None:
   335→        _print_objective_drained_banner(frozen_strict, remaining, breakdown)
   336→
   337→
   338→def show_score_with_plan_context(state: dict, prev) -> None:
   339→    """Load plan (best-effort) and show frozen or live score context.
   340→
   341→    Encapsulates the common load_plan + PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS + reveal
   342→    choreography so command modules don't each repeat it.
   343→    """
   344→    try:
   345→        plan = plan_mod.load_plan()
   346→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   347→        plan = None
   348→    print_execution_or_reveal(state, prev, plan)
   349→
   350→
   351→__all__ = [
   352→    "QueueBreakdown",
   353→    "format_plan_delta",
   354→    "format_queue_block",
   355→    "format_queue_headline",
   356→    "get_plan_start_strict",
   357→    "plan_aware_queue_breakdown",
   358→    "print_execution_or_reveal",
   359→    "print_frozen_score_with_queue_context",
   360→    "show_score_with_plan_context",
   361→]
   362→

   260→        payload.pop("provisional_until_scan", None)
   261→        payload.pop("integrity_penalty", None)
   262→        payload.pop("components", None)
   263→        payload.pop("component_scores", None)
   264→        expired += 1
   265→    return expired
   266→
   267→
   268→def prepare_scan_runtime(args) -> ScanRuntime:
   269→    """Resolve state/config/language and apply scan-time runtime settings."""
   270→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   271→    state_file = runtime.state_path
   272→    state = runtime.state if isinstance(runtime.state, dict) else {}
   273→    state_mod.ensure_state_defaults(state)
   274→    path = Path(args.path)
   275→    config = runtime.config if isinstance(runtime.config, dict) else {}
   276→    lang_config = resolve_lang(args)
   277→    reset_subjective_count = 0
   278→    expired_manual_override_count = _expire_provisional_manual_override_assessments(
   279→        state
   280→    )
   281→    if getattr(args, "reset_subjective", False):
   282→        reset_subjective_count = _reset_subjective_assessments_for_scan_reset(
   283→            state,
   284→            lang_name=getattr(lang_config, "name", None),
   285→        )
   286→
   287→    include_slow = not getattr(args, "skip_slow", False)
   288→    profile = _resolve_scan_profile(getattr(args, "profile", None), lang_config)
   289→    effective_include_slow = _effective_include_slow(include_slow, profile)
   290→
   291→    lang = _configure_lang_runtime(args, config, state, lang_config)
   292→    coverage_warnings = _seed_runtime_coverage_warnings(lang)
   293→    zone_overrides_raw = config.get("zone_overrides")
   294→    zone_overrides = zone_overrides_raw if isinstance(zone_overrides_raw, dict) else None
   295→
   296→    return ScanRuntime(
   297→        args=args,
   298→        state_path=state_file,
   299→        state=state,
   300→        path=path,
   301→        config=config,
   302→        lang=lang,
   303→        lang_label=f" ({lang.name})" if lang else "",
   304→        profile=profile,
   305→        effective_include_slow=effective_include_slow,
   306→        zone_overrides=zone_overrides,
   307→        reset_subjective_count=reset_subjective_count,
   308→        expired_manual_override_count=expired_manual_override_count,
   309→        coverage_warnings=coverage_warnings,
   310→    )
   311→
   312→
   313→def _augment_with_stale_exclusion_issues(
   314→    issues: list[dict[str, Any]],
   315→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   316→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   317→    """Append stale exclude issues when excluded dirs are unreferenced."""
   318→    extra_exclusions = get_exclusions()
   319→    if not (extra_exclusions and runtime.lang and runtime.lang.file_finder):
   320→        return issues
   321→
   322→    scanned_files = runtime.lang.file_finder(runtime.path)
   323→    stale = _audit_excluded_dirs(
   324→        extra_exclusions, scanned_files, get_project_root()
   325→    )
   326→    if not stale:
   327→        return issues
   328→
   329→    augmented = list(issues)
   330→    augmented.extend(stale)
   331→    for stale_issue in stale:
   332→        print(colorize(f"  ℹ {stale_issue['summary']}", "dim"))
   333→    return augmented
   334→
   335→
   336→def _augment_with_stale_wontfix_issues(
   337→    issues: list[dict[str, Any]],
   338→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   339→    *,
   340→    decay_scans: int,
   341→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], int]:
   342→    """Append re-triage issues for stale/worsening wontfix debt."""
   343→    return _augment_stale_wontfix_impl(
   344→        issues,
   345→        state=runtime.state,
   346→        scan_path=runtime.path,
   347→        project_root=get_project_root(),
   348→        decay_scans=decay_scans,
   349→    )
   350→
   351→
   352→def run_scan_generation(
   353→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   354→) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, object], dict[str, object] | None]:
   355→    """Run detector pipeline and return issues, potentials, and codebase metrics."""
   356→    enable_file_cache()
   357→    enable_parse_cache()
   358→    try:
   359→        issues, potentials = plan_mod.generate_issues(
   360→            runtime.path,
   361→            lang=runtime.lang,
   362→            options=PlanScanOptions(
   363→                include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   364→                zone_overrides=runtime.zone_overrides,
   365→                profile=runtime.profile,
   366→            ),
   367→        )
   368→    finally:
   369→        disable_parse_cache()
   370→        disable_file_cache()
   371→
   372→    codebase_metrics = _collect_codebase_metrics(runtime.lang, runtime.path)
   373→    _warn_explicit_lang_with_no_files(
   374→        runtime.args, runtime.lang, runtime.path, codebase_metrics
   375→    )
   376→    issues = _augment_with_stale_exclusion_issues(issues, runtime)
   377→    decay_scans = _coerce_int(
   378→        runtime.config.get("wontfix_decay_scans"),
   379→        default=_WONTFIX_DECAY_SCANS_DEFAULT,
   380→    )
   381→    issues, monitored_wontfix = _augment_with_stale_wontfix_issues(
   382→        issues,
   383→        runtime,
   384→        decay_scans=max(decay_scans, 0),
   385→    )
   386→    potentials["stale_wontfix"] = monitored_wontfix
   387→    return issues, potentials, codebase_metrics
   388→
   389→
   390→def merge_scan_results(
   391→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   392→    issues: list[dict[str, Any]],
   393→    potentials: dict[str, object],
   394→    codebase_metrics: dict[str, object] | None,
   395→) -> ScanMergeResult:
   396→    """Merge issues into persistent state and return diff + previous score snapshot."""
   397→    scan_path_rel = rel(str(runtime.path))
   398→    prev_scan_path = runtime.state.get("scan_path")
   399→    path_changed = prev_scan_path is not None and prev_scan_path != scan_path_rel
   400→
   401→    if not path_changed:
   402→        prev = state_mod.score_snapshot(runtime.state)
   403→    else:
   404→        prev = state_mod.ScoreSnapshot(None, None, None, None)
   405→    prev_dim_scores = (
   406→        runtime.state.get("dimension_scores", {}) if not path_changed else {}
   407→    )
   408→
   409→    if runtime.lang and runtime.lang.zone_map is not None:
   410→        runtime.state["zone_distribution"] = runtime.lang.zone_map.counts()
   411→    _persist_scan_coverage(runtime.state, runtime.lang)
   412→
   413→    target_score = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config, fallback=95.0)
   414→
   415→    diff = state_mod.merge_scan(
   416→        runtime.state,
   417→        issues,
   418→        options=state_mod.MergeScanOptions(
   419→            lang=runtime.lang.name if runtime.lang else None,
   420→            scan_path=scan_path_rel,
   421→            force_resolve=getattr(runtime.args, "force_resolve", False),
   422→            exclude=get_exclusions(),
   423→            potentials=potentials,
   424→            codebase_metrics=codebase_metrics,
   425→            include_slow=runtime.effective_include_slow,
   426→            ignore=runtime.config.get("ignore", []),
   427→            subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   428→        ),
   429→    )
   430→
   431→    expire_stale_holistic(
   432→        runtime.state, runtime.config.get("holistic_max_age_days", 30)
   433→    )
   434→    state_mod.save_state(
   435→        runtime.state,
   436→        runtime.state_path,
   437→        subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   438→    )
   439→
   440→    _clear_needs_rescan_flag(runtime.config)
   441→    _reconcile_plan_post_scan(runtime)
   442→
   443→    return ScanMergeResult(
   444→        diff=diff,
   445→        prev_overall=prev.overall,
   446→        prev_objective=prev.objective,
   447→        prev_strict=prev.strict,
   448→        prev_verified=prev.verified,
   449→        prev_dim_scores=prev_dim_scores,
   450→    )
   451→
   452→
   453→def resolve_noise_snapshot(
   454→    state: state_mod.StateModel,
   455→    config: dict[str, object],
   456→) -> ScanNoiseSnapshot:
   457→    """Resolve noise budget settings and hidden issue counters."""
   458→    noise_budget, global_noise_budget, budget_warning = (
   459→        state_mod.resolve_issue_noise_settings(config)
   460→    )
   461→    issues_by_id = _state_issues(state)
   462→    open_issues = [
   463→        issue
   464→        for issue in state_mod.path_scoped_issues(
   465→            issues_by_id, state.get("scan_path")
   466→        ).values()
   467→        if issue.get("status") == "open"
   468→    ]
   469→    _, hidden_by_detector = state_mod.apply_issue_noise_budget(
   470→        open_issues,
   471→        budget=noise_budget,
   472→        global_budget=global_noise_budget,
   473→    )
   474→
   475→    return ScanNoiseSnapshot(
   476→        noise_budget=noise_budget,
   477→        global_noise_budget=global_noise_budget,
   478→        budget_warning=budget_warning,
   479→        hidden_by_detector=hidden_by_detector,
   480→        hidden_total=sum(hidden_by_detector.values()),
   481→    )
   482→
   483→
   484→def persist_reminder_history(
   485→    runtime: ScanRuntime,
   486→    narrative: dict[str, object],
   487→) -> None:
   488→    """Persist reminder history emitted by narrative computation."""
   489→    if not (narrative and "reminder_history" in narrative):
   490→        return
   491→
   492→    runtime.state["reminder_history"] = narrative["reminder_history"]
   493→    target_score = target_strict_score_from_config(runtime.config, fallback=95.0)
   494→    state_mod.save_state(
   495→        runtime.state,
   496→        runtime.state_path,
   497→        subjective_integrity_target=target_score,
   498→    )
   499→
   500→
   501→__all__ = [
   502→    "ScanStateContractError",
   503→    "ScanMergeResult",
   504→    "ScanNoiseSnapshot",
   505→    "ScanRuntime",
   506→    "merge_scan_results",
   507→    "persist_reminder_history",
   508→    "prepare_scan_runtime",
   509→    "resolve_noise_snapshot",
   510→    "run_scan_generation",
   511→]

     8→from desloppify import languages as lang_api
     9→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.lang import resolve_lang, resolve_lang_settings
    10→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.runtime import command_runtime
    11→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.runtime_options import (
    12→    LangRuntimeOptionsError,

    20→
    21→def _resolve_detector_key(
    22→    detector: str, detect_commands: dict[str, object]
    23→) -> str | None:
    24→    """Resolve detector input to a command key."""
    25→    detector = detector.strip()
    26→    if detector in detect_commands:
    27→        return detector
    28→
    29→    normalized = detector.lower().replace("-", "_")
    30→    if normalized in detect_commands:
    31→        return normalized
    32→
    33→    denormalized = detector.lower().replace("_", "-")
    34→    if denormalized in detect_commands:
    35→        return denormalized
    36→
    37→    return None
    38→
    39→
    40→def cmd_detect(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    41→    """Run a single detector directly (bypass state tracking)."""
    42→    detector_input = args.detector
    43→
    44→    # Resolve language (from --lang flag or auto-detection)
    45→    lang_cfg = resolve_lang(args)
    46→
    47→    if not lang_cfg:
    48→        langs = ", ".join(lang_api.available_langs()) or "registered language plugins"
    49→        raise CommandError(
    50→            f"No language specified. Use --lang <name> (available: {langs})."
    51→        )
    52→
    53→    # Validate detector name
    54→    detector = _resolve_detector_key(detector_input, lang_cfg.detect_commands)
    55→    if detector is None:
    56→        available = ", ".join(sorted(lang_cfg.detect_commands))
    57→        raise CommandError(
    58→            f"Unknown detector for {lang_cfg.name}: {detector_input}\n"
    59→            f"  Available: {available}"
    60→        )
    61→
    62→    # Set default thresholds for detectors that expect them
    63→    if getattr(args, "threshold", None) is None:
    64→        if detector == "large":
    65→            args.threshold = lang_cfg.large_threshold
    66→        elif detector == "dupes":
    67→            args.threshold = 0.8
    68→
    69→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
    70→    lang_settings = resolve_lang_settings(runtime.config, lang_cfg)
    71→    try:
    72→        lang_options = resolve_lang_runtime_options(args, lang_cfg)
    73→    except LangRuntimeOptionsError as exc:
    74→        print_lang_runtime_options_error(exc, lang_name=lang_cfg.name)
    75→        raise CommandError(str(exc), exit_code=2) from exc
    76→    lang = lang_runtime.make_lang_run(
    77→        lang_cfg,
    78→        overrides=lang_runtime.LangRunOverrides(
    79→            runtime_settings=lang_settings,
    80→            runtime_options=lang_options,
    81→        ),
    82→    )
    83→    args.lang_runtime_options = dict(lang_options)
    84→    try:
    85→        lang.detect_commands[detector](args)
    86→    finally:
    87→        args.lang_runtime_options = None
    88→    if not getattr(args, "json", False):
    89→        scan_path = getattr(args, "path", ".") or "."
    90→        print(
    91→            colorize(f"\n  Next command: `desloppify scan --path {scan_path}`", "dim"),
    92→            file=sys.stderr,
    93→        )
    94→

    25→    """Resolve the effective state file path for a command runtime."""
    26→    state_file = runtime.state_path
    27→    if isinstance(state_file, Path):
    28→        return state_file
    29→    return state_mod.STATE_FILE
    30→
    31→
    32→def _prune_excluded_issues(state: dict, pattern: str) -> list[str]:
    33→    """Drop issues whose file path matches a new exclusion pattern."""
    34→    issues = state.get("issues")
    35→    if not isinstance(issues, dict):
    36→        return []
    37→
    38→    removed_ids = [
    39→        issue_id
    40→        for issue_id, issue in issues.items()
    41→        if isinstance(issue, dict)
    42→        and matches_exclusion(str(issue.get("file", "")), pattern)
    43→    ]
    44→    for issue_id in removed_ids:
    45→        issues.pop(issue_id, None)
    46→    return removed_ids
    47→
    48→
    49→def _purge_removed_ids_from_plan(state_file: Path, removed_ids: list[str]) -> int:
    50→    """Remove pruned issue IDs from queue/skips/clusters in plan.json."""
    51→    if not removed_ids:
    52→        return 0
    53→    plan_file = plan_path_for_state(state_file)
    54→    plan = load_plan(plan_file)
    55→    purged = purge_ids(plan, removed_ids)
    56→    if purged:
    57→        save_plan(plan, plan_file)
    58→    return purged
    59→
    60→
    61→def cmd_exclude(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    62→    """Add a path pattern to the exclude list and clean cached queue/state."""
    63→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
    64→    config = runtime.config
    65→    state = runtime.state
    66→    state_file = _state_file_for_runtime(runtime)
    67→
    68→    config_mod.add_exclude_pattern(config, args.pattern)
    69→    config["needs_rescan"] = True
    70→    try:
    71→        config_mod.save_config(config)
    72→    except OSError as exc:
    73→        raise CommandError(f"could not save config: {exc}") from exc
    74→
    75→    removed_ids: list[str] = []
    76→    plan_purged = 0
    77→    if state_file.exists():
    78→        removed_ids = _prune_excluded_issues(state, args.pattern)
    79→        if removed_ids:
    80→            try:
    81→                state_mod.save_state(state, state_file)
    82→            except OSError as exc:
    83→                raise CommandError(f"could not save state: {exc}") from exc
    84→
    85→            try:
    86→                plan_purged = _purge_removed_ids_from_plan(state_file, removed_ids)
    87→            except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
    88→                print(
    89→                    colorize("  Warning: could not update living plan.", "yellow"),
    90→                    file=sys.stderr,
    91→                )
    92→
    93→    print(colorize(f"Added exclude pattern: {args.pattern}", "green"))
    94→    if removed_ids:
    95→        print(f"  Removed {len(removed_ids)} matching issues from state.")
    96→        if plan_purged:
    97→            print(
    98→                colorize(
    99→                    f"  Plan updated: {plan_purged} item(s) removed from queue.",
   100→                    "dim",
   101→                )
   102→            )
   103→    config_warning = check_config_staleness(config)
   104→    if config_warning:
   105→        print(colorize(f"  {config_warning}", "yellow"))
   106→
   107→
   108→__all__ = ["cmd_exclude"]

1→"""Coupling analysis: boundary violations and boundary candidates.
     2→
     3→These detect architectural violations in codebases with shared/tools structure.
     4→The algorithms work on any dep graph — the boundary definitions (what prefixes
     5→constitute "shared" vs "tools") are provided by the caller.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→import logging
     9→from dataclasses import dataclass
    10→from pathlib import Path
    11→
    12→from desloppify.base.discovery.api import rel
    13→from desloppify.base.output.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
    14→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import count_lines, resolve_scan_file
    15→
    16→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    17→
    18→
    19→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    20→class CouplingEdgeCounts:
    21→    """Explicit coupling-edge counters.
    22→
    23→    `eligible_edges` tracks the denominator universe for a detector.
    24→    `violating_edges` tracks only edges that violate the rule.
    25→    """
    26→
    27→    violating_edges: int = 0
    28→    eligible_edges: int = 0
    29→
    30→
    31→def _norm_path(path: str) -> str:
    32→    """Normalize path separators for cross-platform prefix matching."""
    33→    return path.replace("\\", "/")
    34→
    35→
    36→def _norm_prefix(prefix: str, *, name: str) -> str:
    37→    """Normalize a directory prefix and ensure trailing slash."""
    38→    p = _norm_path(str(prefix).strip())
    39→    if not p:
    40→        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-empty directory prefix")
    41→    return p if p.endswith("/") else p + "/"
    42→
    43→
    44→def _norm_root(path: Path) -> str:
    45→    """Normalize project root path for absolute/relative prefix matching."""
    46→    try:
    47→        root = _norm_path(str(path.resolve()))
    48→    except OSError:
    49→        root = _norm_path(str(path))
    50→    return root if root.endswith("/") else root + "/"
    51→
    52→
    53→def _rel_to_root(value: str, root_norm: str) -> str:
    54→    """Return root-relative variant (best effort) for path/prefix matching."""
    55→    if value.startswith(root_norm):
    56→        return value[len(root_norm) :]
    57→    return value.lstrip("/")
    58→
    59→
    60→def _matches_prefix(value: str, prefix: str, *, root_norm: str) -> bool:
    61→    """Match value against prefix regardless of abs/rel shape."""
    62→    if value.startswith(prefix):
    63→        return True
    64→    return _rel_to_root(value, root_norm).startswith(_rel_to_root(prefix, root_norm))
    65→
    66→
    67→def _strip_prefix(value: str, prefix: str, *, root_norm: str) -> str:
    68→    """Strip prefix from value while tolerating abs/rel shape differences."""
    69→    if value.startswith(prefix):
    70→        return value[len(prefix) :]
    71→    value_rel = _rel_to_root(value, root_norm)
    72→    prefix_rel = _rel_to_root(prefix, root_norm)
    73→    if value_rel.startswith(prefix_rel):
    74→        return value_rel[len(prefix_rel) :]
    75→    return value
    76→
    77→
    78→def detect_coupling_violations(
    79→    path: Path, graph: dict, shared_prefix: str, tools_prefix: str
    80→) -> tuple[list[dict], CouplingEdgeCounts]:
    81→    """Find files in shared/ that import from tools/ (backwards coupling)."""
    82→    shared_prefix_norm = _norm_prefix(shared_prefix, name="shared_prefix")
    83→    tools_prefix_norm = _norm_prefix(tools_prefix, name="tools_prefix")
    84→    root_norm = _norm_root(path)
    85→
    86→    violating_edges = 0
    87→    eligible_edges = 0
    88→    entries = []
    89→    for filepath, entry in graph.items():
    90→        filepath_norm = _norm_path(filepath)
    91→        if not _matches_prefix(filepath_norm, shared_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm):
    92→            continue
    93→        for target in entry["imports"]:
    94→            target_norm = _norm_path(target)
    95→            if _matches_prefix(target_norm, tools_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm):
    96→                violating_edges += 1
    97→                eligible_edges += 1
    98→                remainder = _strip_prefix(
    99→                    target_norm, tools_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm
   100→                )
   101→                tool = remainder.split("/")[0] if "/" in remainder else remainder
   102→                entries.append(
   103→                    {
   104→                        "file": filepath,
   105→                        "target": rel(target),
   106→                        "tool": tool,
   107→                        "direction": "shared→tools",
   108→                    }
   109→                )
   110→            elif _matches_prefix(target_norm, shared_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm):
   111→                eligible_edges += 1
   112→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: (e["file"], e["target"])), CouplingEdgeCounts(
   113→        violating_edges=violating_edges,
   114→        eligible_edges=eligible_edges,
   115→    )
   116→
   117→
   118→def detect_boundary_candidates(
   119→    path: Path,
   120→    graph: dict,
   121→    shared_prefix: str,
   122→    tools_prefix: str,
   123→    skip_basenames: set[str] | None = None,
   124→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   125→    """Find shared/ files whose importers ALL come from a single tool."""
   126→    shared_prefix_norm = _norm_prefix(shared_prefix, name="shared_prefix")
   127→    tools_prefix_norm = _norm_prefix(tools_prefix, name="tools_prefix")
   128→    root_norm = _norm_root(path)
   129→    ui_prefix_norm = shared_prefix_norm + "components/ui/"
   130→
   131→    total_shared = 0
   132→    entries = []
   133→    skip_basenames = skip_basenames or set()
   134→    for filepath, entry in graph.items():
   135→        filepath_norm = _norm_path(filepath)
   136→        if not _matches_prefix(filepath_norm, shared_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm):
   137→            continue
   138→        total_shared += 1
   139→        basename = Path(filepath).name
   140→        if basename in skip_basenames:
   141→            continue
   142→        if _matches_prefix(filepath_norm, ui_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm):
   143→            continue
   144→        if entry["importer_count"] == 0:
   145→            continue
   146→
   147→        tool_areas = set()
   148→        has_non_tool_importer = False
   149→        for imp in entry["importers"]:
   150→            imp_norm = _norm_path(imp)
   151→            if _matches_prefix(imp_norm, tools_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm):
   152→                remainder = _strip_prefix(
   153→                    imp_norm, tools_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm
   154→                )
   155→                tool = remainder.split("/")[0]
   156→                tool_areas.add(tool)
   157→            else:
   158→                has_non_tool_importer = True
   159→
   160→        if len(tool_areas) == 1 and not has_non_tool_importer:
   161→            try:
   162→                resolved = resolve_scan_file(filepath, scan_root=path)
   163→                if not resolved.exists():
   164→                    raise FileNotFoundError(resolved)
   165→                loc = count_lines(resolved)
   166→            except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
   167→                log_best_effort_failure(
   168→                    logger,
   169→                    f"read coupling detector candidate {filepath}",
   170→                    exc,
   171→                )
   172→                continue
   173→            entries.append(
   174→                {
   175→                    "file": filepath,
   176→                    "sole_tool": f"src/tools/{list(tool_areas)[0]}",
   177→                    "importer_count": entry["importer_count"],
   178→                    "loc": loc,
   179→                }
   180→            )
   181→
   182→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: -e["loc"]), total_shared
   183→
   184→
   185→def detect_cross_tool_imports(
   186→    path: Path, graph: dict, tools_prefix: str
   187→) -> tuple[list[dict], CouplingEdgeCounts]:
   188→    """Find tools/A files that import from tools/B (cross-tool coupling)."""
   189→    tools_prefix_norm = _norm_prefix(tools_prefix, name="tools_prefix")
   190→    root_norm = _norm_root(path)
   191→
   192→    violating_edges = 0
   193→    eligible_edges = 0
   194→    entries = []
   195→    for filepath, entry in graph.items():
   196→        filepath_norm = _norm_path(filepath)
   197→        if not _matches_prefix(filepath_norm, tools_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm):
   198→            continue
   199→        remainder = _strip_prefix(filepath_norm, tools_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm)
   200→        if "/" not in remainder:
   201→            continue
   202→        source_tool = remainder.split("/")[0]
   203→        for target in entry["imports"]:
   204→            target_norm = _norm_path(target)
   205→            if not _matches_prefix(target_norm, tools_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm):
   206→                continue
   207→            target_tool = _strip_prefix(
   208→                target_norm, tools_prefix_norm, root_norm=root_norm
   209→            ).split("/")[0]
   210→            eligible_edges += 1
   211→            if source_tool != target_tool:
   212→                violating_edges += 1
   213→                entries.append(
   214→                    {
   215→                        "file": filepath,
   216→                        "target": rel(target),
   217→                        "source_tool": source_tool,
   218→                        "target_tool": target_tool,
   219→                        "direction": "tools→tools",
   220→                    }
   221→                )
   222→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: (e["source_tool"], e["file"])), CouplingEdgeCounts(
   223→        violating_edges=violating_edges,
   224→        eligible_edges=eligible_edges,
   225→    )
   226→

1→"""langs command: list all available language plugins with depth and tools."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import argparse
     6→import logging
     7→
     8→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     9→from desloppify.languages._framework import registry_state
    10→from desloppify.languages._framework.base.types import LangConfig
    11→from desloppify.languages._framework.discovery import load_all
    12→from desloppify.languages._framework.generic import SHARED_PHASE_LABELS
    13→from desloppify.languages._framework.resolution import make_lang_config
    14→
    15→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    16→
    17→_DEPTH_BARS = {
    18→    "full": 8,
    19→    "standard": 5,
    20→    "shallow": 3,
    21→    "minimal": 2,
    22→}
    23→
    24→_DEPTH_MAX = 8
    25→
    26→
    27→def _depth_bar(depth: str) -> str:
    28→    """Render a depth bar like ████░░░░."""
    29→    filled = _DEPTH_BARS.get(depth, 2)
    30→    empty = _DEPTH_MAX - filled
    31→    return "\u2588" * filled + "\u2591" * empty
    32→
    33→
    34→def _get_tool_labels(cfg: LangConfig) -> str:
    35→    """Extract tool labels from phases."""
    36→    if cfg.integration_depth == "full":
    37→        return "custom detectors"
    38→    labels = [p.label for p in cfg.phases if p.label not in SHARED_PHASE_LABELS]
    39→    suffix = " (auto-fix)" if cfg.fixers else ""
    40→    return (", ".join(labels) if labels else "none") + suffix
    41→
    42→
    43→def cmd_langs(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    44→    """List all available languages with depth and tool info."""
    45→    load_all()
    46→
    47→    configs: list[tuple[str, LangConfig]] = []
    48→    for name, obj in sorted(registry_state.all_items()):
    49→        if isinstance(obj, LangConfig):
    50→            configs.append((name, obj))
    51→        else:
    52→            try:
    53→                cfg = make_lang_config(name, obj)
    54→                configs.append((name, cfg))
    55→            except (TypeError, ValueError, KeyError, AttributeError) as exc:
    56→                logger.debug("Skipping unresolvable lang config %s: %s", name, exc)
    57→                continue
    58→
    59→    # Sort: full first, then standard, shallow, minimal; alphabetical within
    60→    depth_order = {"full": 0, "standard": 1, "shallow": 2, "minimal": 3}
    61→    configs.sort(key=lambda x: (depth_order.get(x[1].integration_depth, 9), x[0]))
    62→
    63→    # Column widths
    64→    name_width = max(len(name) for name, _ in configs) + 2 if configs else 14
    65→    name_width = max(name_width, 14)
    66→
    67→    print()
    68→    header = f"{'Language':<{name_width}}{'Depth':<14}Tools"
    69→    print(colorize(header, "bold"))
    70→    print("\u2500" * 60)
    71→
    72→    for name, cfg in configs:
    73→        depth = getattr(cfg, "integration_depth", "full")
    74→        bar = _depth_bar(depth)
    75→        tools = _get_tool_labels(cfg)
    76→        print(f"{name:<{name_width}}{bar}    {tools}")
    77→    print()
    78→

1→"""Developer utilities."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import argparse
     6→import ast
     7→import keyword
     8→import re
     9→
    10→from desloppify.app.commands.dev_scaffold_templates import build_scaffold_files
    11→from desloppify.base.discovery.api import safe_write_text
    12→from desloppify.base.exception_sets import CommandError
    13→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
    14→from desloppify.base.text.text_api import get_project_root
    15→
    16→
    17→def cmd_dev(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    18→    """Dispatch developer subcommands."""
    19→    action = getattr(args, "dev_action", None)
    20→    if action == "scaffold-lang":
    21→        try:
    22→            _cmd_scaffold_lang(args)
    23→        except ValueError as ex:
    24→            raise CommandError(str(ex)) from ex
    25→        return
    26→    raise CommandError("Unknown dev action. Use `desloppify dev scaffold-lang`.")
    27→
    28→
    29→def _normalize_lang_name(raw: str) -> str:
    30→    name = raw.strip().lower().replace("-", "_")
    31→    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_]*", name):
    32→        raise ValueError("language name must match [a-z][a-z0-9_]*")
    33→    if keyword.iskeyword(name):
    34→        raise ValueError(f"language name cannot be a Python keyword: {name}")
    35→    return name
    36→
    37→
    38→def _normalize_extensions(values: list[str] | None) -> list[str]:
    39→    out: list[str] = []
    40→    for val in values or []:
    41→        ext = val.strip()
    42→        if not ext:
    43→            continue
    44→        if not ext.startswith("."):
    45→            ext = "." + ext
    46→        if not re.fullmatch(r"\.[a-z0-9]+", ext):
    47→            raise ValueError(f"invalid extension: {val!r}")
    48→        out.append(ext)
    49→    if not out:
    50→        raise ValueError("at least one --extension is required")
    51→    seen: set[str] = set()
    52→    deduped: list[str] = []
    53→    for ext in out:
    54→        if ext not in seen:
    55→            seen.add(ext)
    56→            deduped.append(ext)
    57→    return deduped
    58→
    59→
    60→def _normalize_markers(values: list[str] | None) -> list[str]:
    61→    out: list[str] = []
    62→    for val in values or []:
    63→        marker = val.strip()
    64→        if marker and marker not in out:
    65→            out.append(marker)
    66→    return out
    67→
    68→
    69→def _class_name(lang_name: str) -> str:
    70→    return "".join(part.capitalize() for part in lang_name.split("_")) + "Config"
    71→
    72→
    73→def _template_files(
    74→    lang_name: str,
    75→    extensions: list[str],
    76→    markers: list[str],
    77→    default_src: str,
    78→) -> dict[str, str]:
    79→    class_name = _class_name(lang_name)
    80→    return build_scaffold_files(
    81→        lang_name=lang_name,
    82→        class_name=class_name,
    83→        extensions=extensions,
    84→        markers=markers,
    85→        default_src=default_src,
    86→    )
    87→
    88→
    89→def _render_array(items: list[str]) -> str:
    90→    return ", ".join(repr(x) for x in items)
    91→
    92→
    93→def _append_toml_array_item(text: str, key: str, value: str) -> str:
    94→    pattern = re.compile(
    95→        rf"(^\s*{re.escape(key)}\s*=\s*\[)(.*?)(\]\s*$)",
    96→        re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL,
    97→    )
    98→    match = pattern.search(text)
    99→    if not match:
   100→        return text
   101→
   102→    raw = match.group(2).strip()
   103→    parsed = ast.literal_eval("[" + raw + "]") if raw else []
   104→    if not isinstance(parsed, list):
   105→        return text
   106→    if value in parsed:
   107→        return text
   108→
   109→    parsed.append(value)
   110→    replacement = f"{match.group(1)}{_render_array(parsed)}{match.group(3)}"
   111→    return text[: match.start()] + replacement + text[match.end() :]
   112→
   113→
   114→def _wire_pyproject(lang_name: str) -> bool:
   115→    pyproject_path = get_project_root() / "pyproject.toml"
   116→    if not pyproject_path.is_file():
   117→        return False
   118→
   119→    original = pyproject_path.read_text()
   120→    updated = original
   121→    updated = _append_toml_array_item(
   122→        updated,
   123→        "testpaths",
   124→        f"desloppify/languages/{lang_name}/tests",
   125→    )
   126→
   127→    if updated != original:
   128→        safe_write_text(pyproject_path, updated)
   129→        return True
   130→    return False
   131→
   132→
   133→def _cmd_scaffold_lang(args) -> None:
   134→    raw_name = getattr(args, "name", "")
   135→    lang_name = _normalize_lang_name(raw_name)
   136→    extensions = _normalize_extensions(getattr(args, "extension", None))
   137→    markers = _normalize_markers(getattr(args, "marker", None))
   138→    default_src = getattr(args, "default_src", "src") or "src"
   139→    force = bool(getattr(args, "force", False))
   140→    wire_pyproject = bool(getattr(args, "wire_pyproject", True))
   141→
   142→    lang_dir = get_project_root() / "desloppify" / "languages" / lang_name
   143→    if lang_dir.exists() and not force:
   144→        raise CommandError(
   145→            f"Language directory already exists: {lang_dir}. Use --force to overwrite."
   146→        )
   147→
   148→    files = _template_files(lang_name, extensions, markers, default_src)
   149→    for rel_path, content in files.items():
   150→        target = lang_dir / rel_path
   151→        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   152→        if target.exists() and not force:
   153→            continue
   154→        safe_write_text(target, content)
   155→

1→"""Complexity signal detection: configurable per-language complexity signals."""
     2→
     3→import inspect
     4→import logging
     5→import re
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→
     8→from desloppify.base.output.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
     9→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import resolve_scan_file
    10→
    11→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    12→
    13→
    14→def detect_complexity(
    15→    path: Path, signals, file_finder, threshold: int = 15, min_loc: int = 50
    16→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    17→    """Detect files with complexity signals."""
    18→    files = file_finder(path)
    19→    entries = []
    20→    for filepath in files:
    21→        try:
    22→            p = resolve_scan_file(filepath, scan_root=path)
    23→            content = p.read_text()
    24→            lines = content.splitlines()
    25→            loc = len(lines)
    26→            if loc < min_loc:
    27→                continue
    28→
    29→            file_signals = []
    30→            score = 0
    31→
    32→            for sig in signals:
    33→                try:
    34→                    if sig.compute:
    35→                        # Pass filepath to compute fns that accept it (tree-sitter signals).
    36→                        accepts_filepath = "_filepath" in inspect.signature(
    37→                            sig.compute
    38→                        ).parameters
    39→                        if accepts_filepath:
    40→                            result = sig.compute(content, lines, _filepath=filepath)
    41→                        else:
    42→                            result = sig.compute(content, lines)
    43→                        if result:
    44→                            count, label = result
    45→                            file_signals.append(label)
    46→                            excess = (
    47→                                max(0, count - sig.threshold) if sig.threshold else count
    48→                            )
    49→                            score += excess * sig.weight
    50→                    elif sig.pattern:
    51→                        count = len(re.findall(sig.pattern, content, re.MULTILINE))
    52→                        if count > sig.threshold:
    53→                            file_signals.append(f"{count} {sig.name}")
    54→                            score += (count - sig.threshold) * sig.weight
    55→                except (TypeError, ValueError, KeyError, AttributeError, re.error) as exc:
    56→                    log_best_effort_failure(
    57→                        logger,
    58→                        f"compute complexity signal '{sig.name}' for {filepath}",
    59→                        exc,
    60→                    )
    61→                    continue
    62→
    63→            if file_signals and score >= threshold:
    64→                entries.append(
    65→                    {
    66→                        "file": filepath,
    67→                        "loc": loc,
    68→                        "score": score,
    69→                        "signals": file_signals,
    70→                    }
    71→                )
    72→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
    73→            log_best_effort_failure(
    74→                logger,
    75→                f"read complexity detector candidate {filepath}",
    76→                exc,
    77→            )
    78→            continue
    79→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: -e["score"]), len(files)
    80→
