   339→_DISPLAY_ORDER = list(DISPLAY_ORDER)
   340→
   341→JUDGMENT_DETECTORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
   342→    name for name, meta in DETECTORS.items() if meta.needs_judgment
   343→)
   344→_BASE_DETECTORS: dict[str, DetectorMeta] = dict(DETECTORS)
   345→_BASE_DISPLAY_ORDER: list[str] = list(_DISPLAY_ORDER)
   346→_BASE_JUDGMENT_DETECTORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(JUDGMENT_DETECTORS)
   347→
   348→_on_register_callbacks: list[Callable[[], None]] = []
   349→
   350→
   351→def on_detector_registered(callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
   352→    """Register a callback invoked after register_detector(). No-arg."""
   353→    _on_register_callbacks.append(callback)
   354→
   355→
   356→def register_detector(meta: DetectorMeta) -> None:
   357→    """Register a detector at runtime (used by generic plugins)."""
   358→    global JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   359→    DETECTORS[meta.name] = meta
   360→    if meta.name not in _DISPLAY_ORDER:
   361→        _DISPLAY_ORDER.append(meta.name)
   362→    JUDGMENT_DETECTORS = frozenset(
   363→        name for name, m in DETECTORS.items() if m.needs_judgment
   364→    )
   365→    for cb in _on_register_callbacks:
   366→        cb()
   367→
   368→
   369→def reset_registered_detectors() -> None:
   370→    """Reset runtime-added detector registrations to built-in defaults."""
   371→    global JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   372→    DETECTORS.clear()
   373→    DETECTORS.update(_BASE_DETECTORS)
   374→    _DISPLAY_ORDER.clear()
   375→    _DISPLAY_ORDER.extend(_BASE_DISPLAY_ORDER)
   376→    JUDGMENT_DETECTORS = _BASE_JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   377→    for cb in _on_register_callbacks:
   378→        cb()
   379→
   380→
   381→def detector_names() -> list[str]:
   382→    """All registered detector names, sorted."""
   383→    return sorted(DETECTORS.keys())
   384→
   385→
   386→def display_order() -> list[str]:
   387→    """Canonical display order for terminal output."""
   388→    return list(_DISPLAY_ORDER)
   389→
   390→
   391→_ACTION_PRIORITY = {"auto_fix": 0, "reorganize": 1, "refactor": 2, "manual_fix": 3}
   392→_ACTION_LABELS = {
   393→    "auto_fix": "autofix",
   394→    "reorganize": "move",
   395→    "refactor": "refactor",
   396→    "manual_fix": "manual",
   397→}
   398→
   399→
   400→def dimension_action_type(dim_name: str) -> str:
   401→    """Return a compact action type label for a dimension based on its detectors."""
   402→    best = "manual"
   403→    best_pri = 99
   404→    for d in DETECTORS.values():
   405→        if d.dimension == dim_name:
   406→            pri = _ACTION_PRIORITY.get(d.action_type, 99)
   407→            if pri < best_pri:
   408→                best_pri = pri
   409→                best = d.action_type
   410→    return _ACTION_LABELS.get(best, "manual")
   411→
   412→
   413→def detector_tools() -> dict[str, dict]:
   414→    """Build detector tool metadata keyed by detector name."""
   415→    result = {}
   416→    for name, d in DETECTORS.items():
   417→        entry: dict = {
   418→            "fixers": list(d.fixers),
   419→            "action_type": d.action_type,
   420→        }
   421→        if d.tool:
   422→            entry["tool"] = d.tool
   423→        if d.guidance:
   424→            entry["guidance"] = d.guidance
   425→        result[name] = entry
   426→    return result
   427→

    10→
    11→class FileTextCache:
    12→    """Optional read-through file-text cache used by scan/review passes."""
    13→
    14→    def __init__(self) -> None:
    15→        self._enabled = False
    16→        self._values: dict[str, str | None] = {}
    17→
    18→    def enable(self) -> None:
    19→        self._enabled = True
    20→        self._values.clear()
    21→
    22→    def disable(self) -> None:
    23→        self._enabled = False
    24→        self._values.clear()
    25→
    26→    def read(self, filepath: str) -> str | None:
    27→        if self._enabled and filepath in self._values:
    28→            return self._values[filepath]
    29→
    30→        try:
    31→            content = Path(filepath).read_text(errors="replace")
    32→        except OSError:
    33→            content = None
    34→        if self._enabled:
    35→            self._values[filepath] = content
    36→        return content
    37→
    38→
    39→class SourceFileCache:
    40→    """Small FIFO cache for source-file discovery results."""
    41→
    42→    def __init__(self, *, max_entries: int) -> None:
    43→        self.max_entries = max_entries
    44→        self.values: dict[tuple, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
    45→
    46→    def get(self, key: tuple) -> tuple[str, ...] | None:
    47→        return self.values.get(key)
    48→
    49→    def put(self, key: tuple, value: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
    50→        if len(self.values) >= self.max_entries:
    51→            self.values.pop(next(iter(self.values)))
    52→        self.values[key] = value
    53→
    54→    def clear(self) -> None:
    55→        self.values.clear()
    56→

    62→    exclusions: tuple[str, ...] = ()

    10→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
    11→from desloppify.base.text.text_api import get_project_root
    12→from desloppify.engine.planning.helpers import is_subjective_phase
    13→from desloppify.engine.policy.zones import ZONE_POLICIES, FileZoneMap
    14→from desloppify.languages import auto_detect_lang, available_langs, get_lang

    16→from desloppify.languages._framework.runtime import LangRun, make_lang_run

    19→
    20→@dataclass
    21→class PlanScanOptions:
    22→    """Config object for scan execution behavior."""
    23→
    24→    include_slow: bool = True
    25→    zone_overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None
    26→    profile: str = "full"
    27→
    28→
    29→def _stderr(msg: str) -> None:
    30→    print(colorize(msg, "dim"), file=sys.stderr)
    31→
    32→
    33→def _resolve_lang(
    34→    lang: LangConfig | LangRun | None, project_root: Path
    35→) -> LangConfig | LangRun:
    36→    if lang is not None:
    37→        return lang
    38→
    39→    detected = auto_detect_lang(project_root)
    40→    if detected is None:
    41→        langs = available_langs()
    42→        if not langs:
    43→            raise ValueError("No language plugins available")
    44→        detected = langs[0]
    45→    return get_lang(detected)
    46→
    47→
    48→def _build_zone_map(path: Path, lang: LangRun, zone_overrides: dict[str, str] | None) -> None:
    49→    if not (lang.zone_rules and lang.file_finder):
    50→        return
    51→
    52→    files = lang.file_finder(path)
    53→    lang.zone_map = FileZoneMap(
    54→        files, lang.zone_rules, rel_fn=rel, overrides=zone_overrides
    55→    )
    56→    counts = lang.zone_map.counts()
    57→    zone_str = ", ".join(
    58→        f"{zone}: {count}" for zone, count in sorted(counts.items()) if count > 0
    59→    )
    60→    _stderr(f"  Zones: {zone_str}")
    61→
    62→    from desloppify.languages._framework.generic import capability_report
    63→
    64→    report = capability_report(lang)
    65→    if report is not None:
    66→        present, missing = report
    67→        if present:
    68→            _stderr(f"  Capabilities: {', '.join(present)}")
    69→        if missing:
    70→            _stderr(f"  Not available: {', '.join(missing)}")
    71→
    72→
    73→def _select_phases(lang: LangRun, *, include_slow: bool, profile: str) -> list[DetectorPhase]:
    74→    active_profile = profile if profile in {"objective", "full", "ci"} else "full"
    75→    phases = lang.phases
    76→    if not include_slow or active_profile == "ci":
    77→        phases = [phase for phase in phases if not phase.slow]
    78→    if active_profile in {"objective", "ci"}:
    79→        phases = [phase for phase in phases if not is_subjective_phase(phase)]
    80→    return phases
    81→
    82→
    83→def _run_phases(path: Path, lang: LangRun, phases: list[DetectorPhase]) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
    84→    issues: list[Issue] = []
    85→    all_potentials: dict[str, int] = {}
    86→
    87→    total = len(phases)
    88→    for idx, phase in enumerate(phases, start=1):
    89→        _stderr(f"  [{idx}/{total}] {phase.label}...")
    90→        phase_issues, phase_potentials = phase.run(path, lang)
    91→        all_potentials.update(phase_potentials)
    92→        issues.extend(phase_issues)
    93→
    94→    return issues, all_potentials
    95→
    96→
    97→def _stamp_issue_context(issues: list[Issue], lang: LangRun) -> None:
    98→    if not issues:
    99→        return
   100→
   101→    zone_policies = None
   102→    if lang.zone_map is not None:
   103→        zone_policies = ZONE_POLICIES
   104→
   105→    for issue in issues:
   106→        issue["lang"] = lang.name
   107→        if lang.zone_map is None:
   108→            continue
   109→
   110→        zone = lang.zone_map.get(issue.get("file", ""))
   111→        issue["zone"] = zone.value
   112→        policy = zone_policies.get(zone) if zone_policies else None
   113→        if policy and issue.get("detector") in policy.downgrade_detectors:
   114→            issue["confidence"] = "low"
   115→
   116→
   117→def _generate_issues_from_lang(
   118→    path: Path,
   119→    lang: LangRun,
   120→    *,
   121→    include_slow: bool = True,
   122→    zone_overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None,
   123→    profile: str = "full",
   124→) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   125→    """Run detector phases from a LangRun."""
   126→    _build_zone_map(path, lang, zone_overrides)
   127→    phases = _select_phases(lang, include_slow=include_slow, profile=profile)
   128→    issues, all_potentials = _run_phases(path, lang, phases)
   129→    _stamp_issue_context(issues, lang)
   130→    _stderr(f"\n  Total: {len(issues)} issues")
   131→    return issues, all_potentials
   132→
   133→
   134→def generate_issues(
   135→    path: Path,
   136→    lang: LangConfig | LangRun | None = None,
   137→    *,
   138→    options: PlanScanOptions | None = None,
   139→) -> tuple[list[Issue], dict[str, int]]:
   140→    """Run all detectors and convert results to normalized issues."""
   141→    resolved_options = options or PlanScanOptions()
   142→
   143→    resolved_lang = _resolve_lang(lang, get_project_root())
   144→    runtime_lang = make_lang_run(resolved_lang)
   145→    return _generate_issues_from_lang(
   146→        path,
   147→        runtime_lang,
   148→        include_slow=resolved_options.include_slow,
   149→        zone_overrides=resolved_options.zone_overrides,
   150→        profile=resolved_options.profile,
   151→    )

    46→# Sentinel: "read scan_path from state" (the safe default).

    49→

    51→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    52→class QueueBuildOptions:
    53→    """Configuration for queue construction.
    54→
    55→    ``scan_path`` defaults to reading from ``state["scan_path"]`` so callers
    56→    don't need to thread it manually.  Pass an explicit ``str`` or ``None``
    57→    to override (``None`` disables scope filtering).
    58→    """
    59→
    60→    # Output control
    61→    count: int | None = 1
    62→    explain: bool = False
    63→
    64→    # Scope filtering
    65→    scan_path: str | None | object = _SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE
    66→    scope: str | None = None

    68→    chronic: bool = False
    69→
    70→    # Subjective gating

    72→    subjective_threshold: float = 100.0
    73→    policy: SubjectiveVisibility | None = None
    74→
    75→    # Plan integration
    76→    plan: dict | None = None
    77→    include_skipped: bool = False

    79→
    80→    # Pre-computed context (overrides plan/policy)
    81→    context: QueueContext | None = None
    82→

    84→class WorkQueueResult(TypedDict):
    85→    """Typed shape of the dict returned by :func:`build_work_queue`."""
    86→
    87→    items: list[dict]
    88→    total: int
    89→    grouped: dict[str, list[dict]]
    90→    new_ids: set[str]

    92→
    93→def build_work_queue(
    94→    state: StateModel,
    95→    *,
    96→    options: QueueBuildOptions | None = None,
    97→) -> WorkQueueResult:
    98→    """Build a ranked work queue from state issues.
    99→
   100→    Pipeline:
   101→    1. Gather — issue items, subjective dimensions, workflow stages
   102→    2. Score  — estimate impact from dimension headroom, apply floor
   103→    3. Order  — stamp plan positions, sort, filter to cluster focus
   104→    4. Limit  — truncate to count, optionally add explain metadata
   105→    """
   106→    opts = options or QueueBuildOptions()
   107→    plan, scan_path, status, threshold = _resolve_inputs(opts, state)
   108→
   109→    # 1. Gather
   110→    items = build_issue_items(
   111→        state, scan_path=scan_path, status_filter=status,
   112→        scope=opts.scope, chronic=opts.chronic,
   113→    )
   114→    items += _gather_subjective_items(state, opts, plan, threshold)
   115→    items += _gather_workflow_items(state, plan, status)
   116→
   117→    # 2. Score & filter
   118→    enrich_with_impact(items, state.get("dimension_scores", {}))
   119→    items = [i for i in items if _passes_impact_floor(i)]
   120→
   121→    # 3. Plan-aware ordering
   122→    new_ids, skipped = _plan_presort(items, state, plan)
   123→    items.sort(key=item_sort_key)
   124→    _plan_postsort(items, skipped, plan, opts)
   125→
   126→    # 4. Finalize
   127→    if not items:
   128→        items += _empty_queue_fallback(plan)
   129→    total = len(items)
   130→    if opts.count is not None and opts.count > 0:
   131→        items = items[:opts.count]
   132→    if opts.explain:
   133→        for item in items:
   134→            item["explain"] = item_explain(item)
   135→
   136→    return {
   137→        "items": items,
   138→        "total": total,
   139→        "grouped": group_queue_items(items, "item"),
   140→        "new_ids": new_ids,
   141→    }
   142→
   143→
   144→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   145→# Pipeline helpers (private to this module)
   146→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   147→
   148→
   149→def _resolve_inputs(
   150→    opts: QueueBuildOptions, state: StateModel,
   151→) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None, str, float]:
   152→    """Resolve plan, scan_path, status, and subjective threshold from options."""
   153→    ctx = opts.context
   154→    plan = ctx.plan if ctx is not None else opts.plan
   155→
   156→    scan_path: str | None = (
   157→        state.get("scan_path")
   158→        if opts.scan_path is _SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE
   159→        else opts.scan_path  # type: ignore[assignment]
   160→    )
   161→
   162→    status = opts.status
   163→    if status not in ALL_STATUSES:
   164→        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported status filter: {status}")
   165→
   166→    try:
   167→        threshold = float(opts.subjective_threshold)
   168→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
   169→        threshold = 100.0
   170→    threshold = max(0.0, min(100.0, threshold))
   171→
   172→    return plan, scan_path, status, threshold
   173→
   174→
   175→def _gather_subjective_items(
   176→    state: StateModel,
   177→    opts: QueueBuildOptions,
   178→    plan: dict | None,
   179→    threshold: float,
   180→) -> list[dict]:
   181→    """Build synthetic subjective items, gated by SubjectiveVisibility policy."""
   182→    if not opts.include_subjective:
   183→        return []
   184→    if opts.status not in {"open", "all"}:
   185→        return []
   186→    if opts.chronic:
   187→        return []
   188→
   189→    ctx = opts.context
   190→    policy = (
   191→        (ctx.policy if ctx is not None else None)
   192→        or opts.policy
   193→        or compute_subjective_visibility(state, plan=plan)
   194→    )
   195→
   196→    candidates = build_subjective_items(
   197→        state, state.get("issues", {}), threshold=threshold,
   198→    )
   199→
   200→    # When a plan explicitly includes a subjective item in queue_order,
   201→    # surface it regardless of policy — the plan is authoritative.
   202→    plan_queue_set: set[str] = (
   203→        set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   204→        if plan
   205→        else set()
   206→    )
   207→
   208→    result: list[dict] = []
   209→    for item in candidates:
   210→        if not scope_matches(item, opts.scope):
   211→            continue
   212→        item_id = item.get("id", "")
   213→        if not policy.should_surface(item) and item_id not in plan_queue_set:
   214→            continue
   215→        result.append(item)
   216→    return result

   222→    """Inject triage stages, checkpoints, and create-plan when plan is active."""
   223→    if not plan or status not in {"open", "all"}:

   225→
   226→    items: list[dict] = list(build_triage_stage_items(plan, state))
   227→    for builder in (

   231→    ):

   236→    if plan_item is not None:
   237→        items.append(plan_item)
   238→    return items
   239→

   241→_MIN_STANDALONE_IMPACT = 0.05

   243→
   244→def _passes_impact_floor(item: dict) -> bool:
   245→    """Return True if item should survive the impact floor filter."""
   246→    if item.get("kind") != "issue":
   247→        return True
   248→    if item.get("is_review") or item.get("is_subjective"):
   249→        return True
   250→    impact = item.get("estimated_impact")
   251→    return not impact or impact >= _MIN_STANDALONE_IMPACT
   252→
   253→
   254→def _plan_presort(
   255→    items: list[dict], state: StateModel, plan: dict | None,
   256→) -> tuple[set[str], list[dict]]:
   257→    """Enrich plan metadata and stamp sort keys before sorting.
   258→
   259→    Returns ``(new_ids, skipped)`` — skipped items are removed from
   260→    ``items`` in place and returned separately for post-sort re-append.
   261→    """
   262→    if not plan:
   263→        return set(), []
   264→
   265→    new_ids = _new_item_ids(state)
   266→    enrich_plan_metadata(items, plan)
   267→    stamp_plan_sort_keys(items, plan, new_ids)
   268→    remaining, skipped = separate_skipped(items, plan)
   269→    items[:] = remaining
   270→    return new_ids, skipped
   271→
   272→
   273→def _plan_postsort(
   274→    items: list[dict],
   275→    skipped: list[dict],
   276→    plan: dict | None,
   277→    opts: QueueBuildOptions,
   278→) -> None:
   279→    """Re-append skipped items, stamp positions, filter to cluster focus."""
   280→    if not plan:

   282→

   290→def _empty_queue_fallback(plan: dict | None) -> list[dict]:

   297→    return [{
   298→        "id": "workflow::run-scan",

1→"""Runtime compatibility governance matrix and helper predicates.
     2→
     3→This module is the single source of truth for import-boundary policy:
     4→- public runtime modules (stable entry surfaces),
     5→- deprecated compatibility modules (removal candidates),
     6→- private modules (internal implementation details).
     7→"""
     8→
     9→from __future__ import annotations
    10→
    11→from collections.abc import Iterable
    12→
    13→# Public package roots intended for runtime imports across the codebase.
    14→PUBLIC_RUNTIME_ROOTS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    15→    "desloppify.app",
    16→    "desloppify.base",
    17→    "desloppify.engine",
    18→    "desloppify.intelligence",
    19→    "desloppify.languages",
    20→)
    21→
    22→# Compatibility shims removed from runtime usage; these must not be reintroduced.
    23→SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    24→    {
    25→        "desloppify.utils",
    26→        "desloppify.file_discovery",
    27→        "desloppify.base.output_api",
    28→        "desloppify.base.output_contract",
    29→    }
    30→)
    31→
    32→SOFT_DEPRECATED_SHORT_IMPORTS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    33→    {
    34→        "utils",
    35→        "file_discovery",
    36→    }
    37→)
    38→
    39→# Private internals: only code under these roots may import them directly.
    40→PRIVATE_MODULE_PREFIXES: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    41→PRIVATE_ALLOWED_IMPORTER_PREFIXES: tuple[str, ...] = ("desloppify.base",)
    42→
    43→
    44→def is_soft_deprecated_module(module: str) -> bool:
    45→    """Return True when module is a soft-deprecated compatibility surface."""
    46→    return module in SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES
    47→
    48→
    49→def is_private_module(module: str) -> bool:
    50→    """Return True when module path belongs to a private internal namespace."""
    51→    normalized = module.strip()
    52→    if not normalized:
    53→        return False
    54→    for prefix in PRIVATE_MODULE_PREFIXES:
    55→        if normalized == prefix or normalized.startswith(f"{prefix}."):
    56→            return True
    57→    return False
    58→
    59→
    60→def importer_can_access_private(importer_module: str) -> bool:
    61→    """Return True when importer module is allowed to reference private APIs."""
    62→    normalized = importer_module.strip()
    63→    if not normalized:
    64→        return False
    65→    for prefix in PRIVATE_ALLOWED_IMPORTER_PREFIXES:
    66→        if normalized == prefix or normalized.startswith(f"{prefix}."):
    67→            return True
    68→    return False
    69→
    70→
    71→def iter_soft_deprecated_module_paths() -> Iterable[str]:
    72→    """Yield python-module relative paths for deprecated compatibility modules."""
    73→    for module in sorted(SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES):
    74→        parts = module.split(".")
    75→        yield "/".join(parts) + ".py"
    76→
    77→

     5→
     6→class CommandError(Exception):
     7→    """Raised by command helpers to signal a user-facing CLI error.
     8→
     9→    The CLI entrypoint catches this and prints ``message`` to stderr
    10→    before exiting with ``exit_code``.  Helpers should raise this instead
    11→    of calling ``sys.exit()`` directly so that the error path is testable
    12→    and composable.
    13→    """

    15→    def __init__(self, message: str, *, exit_code: int = 1) -> None:

    45→def resolve_target_strict_score(config: dict | None) -> tuple[int, str | None]:
    46→    """Resolve strict-score target from config with bounded fallback."""
    47→    raw_target = DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE
    48→    if isinstance(config, dict):
    49→        raw_target = config.get("target_strict_score", DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE)
    50→    try:
    51→        target = int(raw_target)
    52→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    53→        return (
    54→            DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE,
    55→            (
    56→                f"Invalid config `target_strict_score={raw_target!r}`; using "
    57→                f"{DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE}"
    58→            ),
    59→        )
    60→    if target < MIN_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE or target > MAX_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE:
    61→        return (
    62→            DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE,
    63→            (
    64→                f"Invalid config `target_strict_score={raw_target!r}`; using "
    65→                f"{DEFAULT_TARGET_STRICT_SCORE}"
    66→            ),
    67→        )
    68→    return target, None
    69→
    70→
    71→def compute_strict_target(strict_score: float | None, config: dict | None) -> StrictTarget:
    72→    """Build strict-target context for command rendering and agents."""
    73→    target, warning = resolve_target_strict_score(config)
    74→    if not isinstance(strict_score, int | float):
    75→        return {
    76→            "target": float(target),
    77→            "current": None,
    78→            "gap": None,
    79→            "state": "unavailable",
    80→            "warning": warning,
    81→        }
    82→
    83→    current = round(float(strict_score), 1)
    84→    gap = round(float(target) - current, 1)
    85→    if gap > 0:
    86→        state = "below"
    87→    elif gap < 0:
    88→        state = "above"
    89→    else:
    90→        state = "at"
    91→    return {
    92→        "target": float(target),
    93→        "current": current,
    94→        "gap": gap,
    95→        "state": state,
    96→        "warning": warning,
    97→    }

   100→def count_open_by_detector(issues: dict) -> dict[str, int]:
   101→    """Count open issues by detector, merging structural sub-detectors."""
   102→    by_detector: dict[str, int] = {}
   103→    for issue in issues.values():
   104→        if issue["status"] != "open" or issue.get("suppressed"):
   105→            continue
   106→        detector = issue.get("detector", "unknown")
   107→        if detector in STRUCTURAL_MERGE:
   108→            detector = "structural"
   109→        by_detector[detector] = by_detector.get(detector, 0) + 1
   110→        if detector == "review" and issue.get("detail", {}).get("holistic"):
   111→            by_detector["review_holistic"] = by_detector.get("review_holistic", 0) + 1
   112→    if by_detector.get("review", 0) > 0:
   113→        by_detector["review_uninvestigated"] = sum(
   114→            1
   115→            for issue in issues.values()
   116→            if issue.get("status") == "open"
   117→            and not issue.get("suppressed")
   118→            and issue.get("detector") == "review"
   119→            and not issue.get("detail", {}).get("investigation")
   120→        )
   121→    return by_detector
   122→
   123→
   124→def resolve_badge_path(project_root: Path) -> tuple[str, Path]:
   125→    """Resolve badge path from config, defaulting to root-level scorecard.png."""
   126→    default_rel = "scorecard.png"
   127→    config = {}
   128→    try:
   129→        config = _load_config()
   130→    except (AttributeError, OSError):
   131→        config = {}
   132→
   133→    raw_path = default_rel
   134→    if isinstance(config, dict):
   135→        config.setdefault("badge_path", default_rel)
   136→        configured = config.get("badge_path")
   137→        if isinstance(configured, str) and configured.strip():
   138→            raw_path = configured.strip()
   139→
   140→    path = Path(raw_path)
   141→    is_root_anchored = bool(path.root)
   142→    if not path.is_absolute() and not is_root_anchored:
   143→        return raw_path, project_root / path
   144→
   145→    try:
   146→        rel_path = str(path.relative_to(project_root))
   147→    except ValueError:
   148→        rel_path = str(path)
   149→    return rel_path, path
   150→
   151→
   152→def compute_badge_status() -> BadgeStatus:
   153→    """Check configured scorecard path and whether README references it."""
   154→    project_root = get_project_root()
   155→    scorecard_rel, scorecard_path = resolve_badge_path(project_root)
   156→    generated = scorecard_path.exists()
   157→
   158→    in_readme = False
   159→    if generated:
   160→        for readme_name in ("README.md", "readme.md", "README.MD"):
   161→            readme_path = project_root / readme_name
   162→            if readme_path.exists():
   163→                try:
   164→                    in_readme = scorecard_rel in readme_path.read_text(
   165→                        encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"
   166→                    )
   167→                except OSError:
   168→                    in_readme = False
   169→                break
   170→
   171→    recommendation = None
   172→    if generated and not in_readme:
   173→        recommendation = f'Add to README: <img src="{scorecard_rel}" width="100%">'
   174→
   175→    return {
   176→        "generated": generated,
   177→        "in_readme": in_readme,
   178→        "path": scorecard_rel,
   179→        "recommendation": recommendation,
   180→    }
   181→
   182→
   183→def compute_primary_action(actions: list[dict]) -> PrimaryAction | None:
   184→    """Pick the highest-priority action for user-facing guidance."""
   185→    if not actions:
   186→        return None
   187→    top = actions[0]
   188→    command = str(top.get("command", "")).strip()
   189→    if not command:
   190→        return None
   191→    description = str(top.get("description", "")).strip() or "run highest-impact action"
   192→    return {
   193→        "command": command,
   194→        "description": description,
   195→    }
   196→
   197→
   198→def compute_why_now(
   199→    phase: str,
   200→    strategy: dict[str, object],
   201→    primary_action: dict | None,
   202→) -> str:
   203→    """Explain why the recommended action should happen now."""
   204→    hint = str(strategy.get("hint", "")).strip() if isinstance(strategy, dict) else ""
   205→    if hint:
   206→        return hint
   207→    if primary_action and primary_action.get("description"):
   208→        return str(primary_action["description"])
   209→    phase_default = {
   210→        "first_scan": "Start with highest-impact issues to establish a clean baseline.",
   211→        "regression": "Recent regressions should be contained before new work.",
   212→        "stagnation": "Current approach is stalling; tackle a different high-impact lane.",
   213→        "maintenance": "Keep the codebase stable by resolving new risk quickly.",
   214→    }
   215→    return phase_default.get(phase, "Address the highest-impact open issues first.")
   216→
   217→
   218→def compute_verification_step(_command: str | None) -> VerificationStep:
   219→    """Verification step returned with every narrative plan."""
   220→    return {
   221→        "command": "desloppify scan",
   222→        "reason": "revalidate after changes",
   223→    }
   224→
   225→
   226→def compute_risk_flags(state: StateModel, debt: dict) -> list[RiskFlag]:
   227→    """Build ordered risk flags from suppression and wontfix debt signals."""
   228→    flags: list[RiskFlag] = []
   229→
   230→    ignore_integrity = state.get("ignore_integrity", {})
   231→    suppressed_pct = float(ignore_integrity.get("suppressed_pct", 0.0) or 0.0)
   232→    ignored_count = int(ignore_integrity.get("ignored", 0) or 0)
   233→    if suppressed_pct >= _HIGH_IGNORE_SUPPRESSION_THRESHOLD or ignored_count >= 100:
   234→        severity = "high" if suppressed_pct >= 40.0 or ignored_count >= 200 else "medium"
   235→        message = (
   236→            f"{suppressed_pct:.1f}% issues hidden by ignore patterns"
   237→            if suppressed_pct > 0
   238→            else f"{ignored_count} issues hidden by ignore patterns"
   239→        )
   240→        flags.append(
   241→            {
   242→                "type": "high_ignore_suppression",
   243→                "severity": severity,
   244→                "message": message,
   245→            }
   246→        )
   247→
   248→    wontfix_count = int(debt.get("wontfix_count", 0) or 0)
   249→    overall_gap = float(debt.get("overall_gap", 0.0) or 0.0)
   250→    if overall_gap >= _WONTFIX_GAP_THRESHOLD or wontfix_count > 0:
   251→        severity = "high" if overall_gap >= 5.0 or wontfix_count >= 50 else "medium"
   252→        flags.append(
   253→            {
   254→                "type": "wontfix_gap",
   255→                "severity": severity,
   256→                "message": (
   257→                    f"Strict/lenient gap is {overall_gap:.1f} pts with "
   258→                    f"{wontfix_count} wontfix issues"
   259→                ),
   260→            }
   261→        )
   262→
   263→    flags.sort(key=lambda flag: _RISK_SEVERITY_ORDER.get(flag.get("severity"), 99))
   264→    return flags
   265→
   266→
   267→def history_for_lang(raw_history: list[dict], lang: str | None) -> list[dict]:
   268→    if not lang:
   269→        return raw_history
   270→    return [entry for entry in raw_history if entry.get("lang") in (lang, None)]
   271→
   272→
   273→def scoped_issues(state: StateModel) -> dict[str, Issue]:
   274→    return path_scoped_issues(
   275→        state.get("issues", {}), state.get("scan_path")
   276→    )

   279→def score_snapshot(state: StateModel) -> tuple[float | None, float | None]:
   280→    scores = state_score_snapshot(state)
   281→    return scores.strict, scores.overall

    43→def cmd_plan_output(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:

    45→    runtime = command_runtime(args)

    58→    output = getattr(args, "output", None)
    59→    if output:

    61→            safe_write_text(output, plan_md)
    62→            print(colorize(f"Plan written to {output}", "green"))
    63→            print_agent_plan(

    67→        except OSError as e:

     8→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.lang import resolve_lang

    10→from desloppify.languages._framework.base.types import FixerConfig, LangConfig
    11→
    12→_COMMAND_POST_FIX: dict[str, Callable[..., None]] = {}

    14→
    15→def _load_fixer(args, fixer_name: str) -> tuple[LangConfig, FixerConfig]:
    16→    """Resolve fixer from language plugin registry, or exit."""
    17→    lang = resolve_lang(args)
    18→    if not lang:
    19→        raise CommandError("Could not detect language. Use --lang to specify.")
    20→    if not lang.fixers:
    21→        raise CommandError(f"No auto-fixers available for {lang.name}.")
    22→    if fixer_name not in lang.fixers:
    23→        available = ", ".join(sorted(lang.fixers.keys()))
    24→        raise CommandError(
    25→            f"Unknown fixer: {fixer_name}\n  Available: {available}"
    26→        )
    27→    fc = lang.fixers[fixer_name]
    28→    if fixer_name in _COMMAND_POST_FIX and not fc.post_fix:
    29→        fc = dataclasses.replace(fc, post_fix=_COMMAND_POST_FIX[fixer_name])
    30→    return lang, fc
    31→

    16→class CommandRuntime:
    17→    """Explicit runtime dependencies shared by command handlers."""
    18→
    19→    config: dict[str, Any]
    20→    state: StateModel

    24→def command_runtime(args) -> CommandRuntime:
    25→    """Return runtime context from explicit args.runtime or construct one."""
    26→    runtime = getattr(args, "runtime", None)
    27→    if isinstance(runtime, CommandRuntime):
    28→        return runtime

    35→    state = state_mod.load_state(state_file)
    36→
    37→    return CommandRuntime(config=config, state=state, state_path=state_file)

    22→def _consecutive_subjective_integrity_status(
    23→    state: StateModel, status: str
    24→) -> int:
    25→    """Return consecutive trailing scans with the given subjective-integrity status."""
    26→    history = state.get("scan_history", [])
    27→    if not isinstance(history, list):
    28→        return 0
    29→
    30→    streak = 0
    31→    for entry in reversed(history):
    32→        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
    33→            break
    34→        integrity = entry.get("subjective_integrity")
    35→        if not isinstance(integrity, dict):
    36→            break
    37→        if integrity.get("status") != status:
    38→            break
    39→        streak += 1
    40→    return streak
    41→
    42→
    43→def _show_score_reveal(
    44→    state: StateModel,
    45→    new: state_mod.ScoreSnapshot,
    46→    *,
    47→    target_strict: float | None = None,
    48→) -> None:
    49→    """Show before/after score comparison when a queue cycle just completed.
    50→
    51→    This fires when the plan had ``plan_start_scores`` and the queue was empty
    52→    at scan time (i.e. the reconcile block cleared plan_start_scores).  We detect
    53→    this by checking the plan *before* the clear happened — since merge_scan_results
    54→    clears it, we peek at the ``_last_score_reveal`` stash it leaves behind.
    55→    """
    56→    # scan_workflow stashes the old plan_start_scores on state as a transient
    57→    # key when it clears them (queue empty).  Pop it here for the reveal.
    58→    plan_start = state.pop("_plan_start_scores_for_reveal", None)
    59→    if not isinstance(plan_start, dict) or not plan_start.get("strict"):
    60→        return
    61→
    62→    old_strict = float(plan_start["strict"])
    63→    new_strict = float(new.strict or 0)
    64→    delta = round(new_strict - old_strict, 1)
    65→    delta_str = f" ({'+' if delta > 0 else ''}{delta:.1f})" if abs(delta) >= 0.05 else ""
    66→
    67→    bar = "=" * 50
    68→    print(colorize(f"  {bar}", "cyan"))
    69→    print(colorize("  SCORE UPDATE — Queue cycle complete!", "bold"))
    70→    print(colorize(f"  Plan-start: strict {old_strict:.1f}/100", "dim"))
    71→    print(colorize(f"  Updated:    strict {new_strict:.1f}/100{delta_str}", "cyan"))
    72→    if target_strict is not None:
    73→        target_gap = round(target_strict - new_strict, 1)
    74→        if target_gap > 0:
    75→            print(colorize(f"  Target:     {target_strict:.1f} (+{target_gap:.1f} to go)", "dim"))
    76→        else:
    77→            print(colorize(f"  Target:     {target_strict:.1f} — reached!", "green"))
    78→    print(colorize(f"  {bar}", "cyan"))

   117→        override_existing or "reset_on_scan" not in payload

   119→        payload["reset_on_scan"] = prompt_meta["reset_on_scan"]
   120→
   121→
   122→def _merge_enabled_by_default_flag(
   123→    payload: dict[str, object],
   124→    *,
   125→    prompt_meta: dict[str, object],
   126→    override_existing: bool,
   127→    default_enabled: bool,
   128→) -> None:
   129→    if default_enabled:
   130→        payload["enabled_by_default"] = True
   131→    if "enabled_by_default" not in prompt_meta:
   132→        return
   133→    prompt_enabled = bool(prompt_meta["enabled_by_default"])
   134→    if override_existing:
   135→        payload["enabled_by_default"] = prompt_enabled
   136→        return
   137→    payload["enabled_by_default"] = bool(
   138→        payload.get("enabled_by_default", False) or prompt_enabled
   139→    )
   140→
   141→
   142→def _normalized_default_dimensions(dimensions: list[str]) -> set[str]:
   143→    return {
   144→        _normalize_dimension_name(dim)
   145→        for dim in dimensions
   146→        if isinstance(dim, str) and dim.strip()
   147→    }
   148→
   149→
   150→def _merge_dimension_meta(
   151→    target: dict[str, dict[str, object]],
   152→    *,
   153→    dimensions: list[str],
   154→    prompts: dict[str, dict[str, object]],
   155→    override_existing: bool = False,
   156→) -> None:
   157→    defaults = _normalized_default_dimensions(dimensions)
   158→
   159→    for raw_dim, entry in prompts.items():
   160→        dim = _normalize_dimension_name(raw_dim)
   161→        if not dim:
   162→            continue
   163→
   164→        payload = target.setdefault(dim, {})
   165→        prompt_meta = extract_prompt_meta(entry)
   166→        _merge_prompt_display_and_weights(
   167→            payload,
   168→            prompt_meta=prompt_meta,
   169→            override_existing=override_existing,
   170→        )
   171→        _merge_enabled_by_default_flag(
   172→            payload,
   173→            prompt_meta=prompt_meta,
   174→            override_existing=override_existing,
   175→            default_enabled=dim in defaults,
   176→        )
   177→
   178→
   179→def _default_available_languages() -> list[str]:
   180→    try:
   181→        return list(_available_langs())
   182→    except (ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError):
   183→        return []
   184→
   185→
   186→def _default_load_dimensions_payload() -> tuple[
   187→    list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str
   188→]:
   189→    return _load_dimensions()
   190→
   191→
   192→def _default_load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(
   193→    lang_name: str,
   194→) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]:
   195→    return _load_dimensions_for_lang(lang_name)
   196→
   197→
   198→class _SubjectiveProviderState:
   199→    def __init__(self) -> None:
   200→        self.available_languages_provider: Callable[[], list[str]] = (
   201→            _default_available_languages
   202→        )
   203→        self.load_dimensions_payload_provider: Callable[
   204→            [], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   205→        ] = _default_load_dimensions_payload
   206→        self.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider: Callable[
   207→            [str], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   208→        ] = _default_load_dimensions_payload_for_lang
   209→
   210→
   211→_PROVIDER_STATE = _SubjectiveProviderState()
   212→
   213→
   214→def _available_languages() -> list[str]:
   215→    return _PROVIDER_STATE.available_languages_provider()
   216→
   217→
   218→def _load_dimensions_payload() -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]:
   219→    return _PROVIDER_STATE.load_dimensions_payload_provider()
   220→
   221→
   222→def _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(
   223→    lang_name: str,
   224→) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]:
   225→    return _PROVIDER_STATE.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider(lang_name)
   226→
   227→
   228→def _clear_subjective_dimension_caches() -> None:
   229→    default_dimension_keys.cache_clear()
   230→    default_dimension_keys_for_lang.cache_clear()
   231→    load_subjective_dimension_metadata.cache_clear()
   232→    load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang.cache_clear()
   233→
   234→
   235→def configure_subjective_dimension_providers(
   236→    *,
   237→    available_languages_provider: Callable[[], list[str]] | None = None,
   238→    load_dimensions_payload_provider: Callable[
   239→        [], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   240→    ]
   241→    | None = None,
   242→    load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider: Callable[
   243→        [str], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   244→    ]
   245→    | None = None,
   246→) -> None:
   247→    """Configure metadata providers for subjective-dimension lookups."""
   248→    state = _PROVIDER_STATE
   249→
   250→    changed = False
   251→    if (
   252→        available_languages_provider is not None
   253→        and available_languages_provider is not state.available_languages_provider
   254→    ):
   255→        state.available_languages_provider = available_languages_provider
   256→        changed = True
   257→    if (
   258→        load_dimensions_payload_provider is not None
   259→        and load_dimensions_payload_provider
   260→        is not state.load_dimensions_payload_provider
   261→    ):
   262→        state.load_dimensions_payload_provider = load_dimensions_payload_provider
   263→        changed = True
   264→    if (
   265→        load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider is not None
   266→        and load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   267→        is not state.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   268→    ):
   269→        state.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider = (
   270→            load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   271→        )
   272→        changed = True
   273→
   274→    if changed:
   275→        _clear_subjective_dimension_caches()
   276→
   277→
   278→def reset_subjective_dimension_providers() -> None:
   279→    """Reset metadata providers to built-in defaults."""
   280→    configure_subjective_dimension_providers(
   281→        available_languages_provider=_default_available_languages,
   282→        load_dimensions_payload_provider=_default_load_dimensions_payload,
   283→        load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider=_default_load_dimensions_payload_for_lang,
   284→    )
   285→
   286→
   287→def _normalize_dimension_list(values: list[str]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   288→    normalized: list[str] = []
   289→    for raw in values:
   290→        if not isinstance(raw, str):
   291→            continue
   292→        dim = _normalize_dimension_name(raw)
   293→        if not dim or dim in normalized:
   294→            continue
   295→        normalized.append(dim)
   296→    return tuple(normalized)
   297→
   298→
   299→@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
   300→def default_dimension_keys() -> tuple[str, ...]:
   301→    """Return canonical default subjective dimension keys."""
   302→    try:
   303→        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
   304→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   305→        logger.debug("Failed to load default subjective dimensions: %s", exc)
   306→        return tuple(_LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.keys())
   307→    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)
   308→
   309→
   310→@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
   311→def default_dimension_keys_for_lang(lang_name: str | None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   312→    """Return default subjective dimension keys for a specific language."""
   313→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   314→    if normalized is None:
   315→        return default_dimension_keys()
   316→    try:
   317→        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(normalized)
   318→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   319→        logger.debug(
   320→            "Failed to load subjective dimensions for lang %s: %s",
   321→            normalized,
   322→            exc,
   323→        )
   324→        return default_dimension_keys()
   325→    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)
   326→
   327→
   328→def _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(
   329→    *,
   330→    lang_name: str | None,
   331→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   332→    out: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
   333→
   334→    try:
   335→        shared_defaults, shared_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
   336→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   337→        logger.debug("Failed to load shared subjective dimension payload: %s", exc)
   338→        shared_defaults, shared_prompts = [], {}
   339→    _merge_dimension_meta(out, dimensions=shared_defaults, prompts=shared_prompts)
   340→
   341→    langs = (
   342→        [lang_name]
   343→        if isinstance(lang_name, str) and lang_name.strip()
   344→        else _available_languages()
   345→    )
   346→    for name in langs:
   347→        try:
   348→            lang_defaults, lang_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(name)
   349→            _merge_dimension_meta(
   350→                out,
   351→                dimensions=lang_defaults,
   352→                prompts=lang_prompts,
   353→                override_existing=bool(lang_name),
   354→            )
   355→        except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   356→            logger.debug("Failed to load dimensions for lang %s: %s", name, exc)
   357→            continue
   358→
   359→    for dim, payload in out.items():
   360→        payload.setdefault(
   361→            "display_name",
   362→            _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.get(dim, _title_display_name(dim)),
   363→        )
   364→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   365→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   366→        if dim in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES:
   367→            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
   368→        else:
   369→            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   370→
   371→    # Preserve legacy dimensions even if a payload temporarily drops one.
   372→    for dim, display in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.items():
   373→        payload = out.setdefault(dim, {})
   374→        payload.setdefault("display_name", display)
   375→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   376→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", True)
   377→        payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
   378→
   379→    return out
   380→
   381→
   382→@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
   383→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata() -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   384→    """Return merged metadata across all known dimensions/languages."""
   385→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=None)
   386→
   387→
   388→@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
   389→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(
   390→    lang_name: str | None,
   391→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   392→    """Return merged metadata for one language (with language overrides)."""
   393→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   394→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=normalized)
   395→
   396→
   397→def _metadata_registry(lang_name: str | None) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   398→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   399→    if normalized is None:
   400→        return load_subjective_dimension_metadata()
   401→    return load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(normalized)
   402→
   403→
   404→def get_dimension_metadata(
   405→    dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None
   406→) -> dict[str, object]:
   407→    """Return metadata for one dimension key (with sane defaults)."""
   408→    dim = _normalize_dimension_name(dimension_name)
   409→    all_meta = _metadata_registry(lang_name)
   410→    payload = dict(all_meta.get(dim, {}))
   411→
   412→    payload.setdefault("display_name", _title_display_name(dim))
   413→    payload.setdefault("weight", 1.0)
   414→    payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   415→    payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   416→    return payload
   417→
   418→
   419→def dimension_display_name(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> str:
   420→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   421→    return str(meta.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dimension_name)))
   422→
   423→
   424→def dimension_weight(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> float:
   425→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   426→    raw = meta.get("weight", 1.0)
   427→    if is_numeric(raw):
   428→        return max(0.0, float(raw))
   429→    return 1.0
   430→
   431→
   432→def default_display_names_map(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
   433→    """Display-name map for default subjective dimensions."""
   434→    out: dict[str, str] = {}
   435→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   436→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   437→            continue
   438→        out[dim] = str(payload.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dim)))
   439→    return out
   440→
   441→
   442→def resettable_default_dimensions(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   443→    """Default subjective dimensions that should be reset by scan reset."""
   444→    out = []
   445→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   446→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   447→            continue
   448→        if not bool(payload.get("reset_on_scan", True)):
   449→            continue
   450→        out.append(dim)
   451→    return tuple(sorted(set(out)))
   452→
   453→
   454→__all__ = [
   455→    "DISPLAY_NAMES",
   456→    "configure_subjective_dimension_providers",
   457→    "default_dimension_keys",
   458→    "default_dimension_keys_for_lang",
   459→    "default_display_names_map",
   460→    "dimension_display_name",

1→"""State-path and scan-gating helpers for command modules."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→
     7→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.lang import auto_detect_lang_name
     8→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     9→from desloppify.base.text.text_api import get_project_root
    10→
    11→
    12→def _sole_existing_lang_state_file() -> Path | None:
    13→    """Return the only existing language-specific state file, if unambiguous."""
    14→    state_dir = get_project_root() / ".desloppify"
    15→    if not state_dir.exists():
    16→        return None
    17→    candidates = sorted(path for path in state_dir.glob("state-*.json") if path.is_file())
    18→    if len(candidates) == 1:
    19→        return candidates[0]
    20→    return None
    21→
    22→
    23→def _allow_lang_state_fallback(args) -> bool:
    24→    """Whether command can safely fallback to the sole existing lang state file."""
    25→    # Scan should always honor detected/explicit language mapping to avoid cross-lang merges.
    26→    return getattr(args, "command", None) != "scan"
    27→
    28→
    29→def state_path(args) -> Path | None:
    30→    """Get state file path from args, or None for default."""
    31→    path_arg = getattr(args, "state", None)
    32→    if path_arg:
    33→        return Path(path_arg)
    34→    lang_name = getattr(args, "lang", None)
    35→    if not lang_name:
    36→        lang_name = auto_detect_lang_name(args)
    37→    if lang_name:
    38→        resolved = get_project_root() / ".desloppify" / f"state-{lang_name}.json"
    39→        if resolved.exists() or not _allow_lang_state_fallback(args):
    40→            return resolved
    41→        fallback = _sole_existing_lang_state_file()
    42→        if fallback is not None:
    43→            return fallback
    44→        return resolved
    45→
    46→    if _allow_lang_state_fallback(args):
    47→        fallback = _sole_existing_lang_state_file()
    48→        if fallback is not None:
    49→            return fallback
    50→    return None
    51→
    52→
    53→def require_completed_scan(state: dict) -> bool:
    54→    """Return True when the state contains at least one completed scan."""
    55→    has_completed_scan = bool(state.get("last_scan"))
    56→    if not has_completed_scan:
    57→        print(colorize("No scans yet. Run: desloppify scan", "yellow"))
    58→    return has_completed_scan
    59→

1→"""Language runtime-option parsing helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import sys
     6→
     7→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     8→
     9→
    10→class LangRuntimeOptionsError(ValueError):
    11→    """Raised when --lang-opt values cannot be parsed or normalized."""
    12→
    13→    def __init__(self, message: str, *, supported_options: list[str] | None = None):
    14→        super().__init__(message)
    15→        self.supported_options = supported_options or []
    16→
    17→
    18→def parse_lang_opt_assignments(raw_values: list[str] | None) -> dict[str, str]:
    19→    """Parse repeated KEY=VALUE --lang-opt inputs."""
    20→    values = raw_values or []
    21→    parsed: dict[str, str] = {}
    22→    for raw in values:
    23→        text = (raw or "").strip()
    24→        if not text:
    25→            continue
    26→        if "=" not in text:
    27→            raise ValueError(f"Invalid --lang-opt '{raw}'. Expected KEY=VALUE.")
    28→        key, value = text.split("=", 1)
    29→        key = key.strip().replace("-", "_")
    30→        if not key:
    31→            raise ValueError(f"Invalid --lang-opt '{raw}'. Missing option key.")
    32→        parsed[key] = value.strip()
    33→    return parsed
    34→
    35→
    36→def resolve_lang_runtime_options(args, lang) -> dict[str, object]:
    37→    """Resolve runtime options from generic --lang-opt inputs."""
    38→    try:
    39→        options = parse_lang_opt_assignments(getattr(args, "lang_opt", None))
    40→    except ValueError as exc:
    41→        raise LangRuntimeOptionsError(str(exc)) from exc
    42→
    43→    try:
    44→        return lang.normalize_runtime_options(options, strict=True)
    45→    except KeyError as exc:
    46→        supported = sorted((lang.runtime_option_specs or {}).keys())
    47→        raise LangRuntimeOptionsError(
    48→            str(exc),
    49→            supported_options=supported,
    50→        ) from exc
    51→
    52→
    53→def print_lang_runtime_options_error(exc: LangRuntimeOptionsError, *, lang_name: str) -> None:
    54→    """Render a runtime-option parse/validation error."""
    55→    print(colorize(f"  {exc}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
    56→    hint = ", ".join(exc.supported_options) if exc.supported_options else "(none)"
    57→    print(
    58→        colorize(f"  Supported {lang_name} runtime options: {hint}", "dim"),
    59→        file=sys.stderr,
    60→    )
    61→
    62→
    63→__all__ = [
    64→    "LangRuntimeOptionsError",
    65→    "parse_lang_opt_assignments",
    66→    "print_lang_runtime_options_error",
    67→    "resolve_lang_runtime_options",
    68→]
    69→

1→"""Centralized score update display for all state-changing commands."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify import state as state_mod
     6→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.score import target_strict_score_from_config
     7→from desloppify.base import config as config_mod
     8→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     9→
    10→
    11→def _format_delta(value: float, prev: float | None) -> tuple[str, str]:
    12→    """Return (delta_str, color) for a score change."""
    13→    delta = value - prev if prev is not None else 0
    14→    delta_str = f" ({'+' if delta > 0 else ''}{delta:.1f})" if delta != 0 else ""
    15→    color = "green" if delta > 0 else ("red" if delta < 0 else "dim")
    16→    return delta_str, color
    17→
    18→
    19→def print_score_update(
    20→    state: dict,
    21→    prev: state_mod.ScoreSnapshot,
    22→    *,
    23→    config: dict | None = None,
    24→    label: str = "Scores",
    25→) -> None:
    26→    """Print score quartet with deltas and strict target progress."""
    27→    new = state_mod.score_snapshot(state)
    28→    if (
    29→        new.overall is None
    30→        or new.objective is None
    31→        or new.strict is None
    32→        or new.verified is None
    33→    ):
    34→        print(colorize(f"\n  {label} unavailable — run `desloppify scan`.", "yellow"))
    35→        return
    36→
    37→    overall_s, overall_c = _format_delta(new.overall, prev.overall)
    38→    objective_s, objective_c = _format_delta(new.objective, prev.objective)
    39→    strict_s, strict_c = _format_delta(new.strict, prev.strict)
    40→    verified_s, verified_c = _format_delta(new.verified, prev.verified)
    41→
    42→    print(
    43→        f"\n  {label}: "
    44→        + colorize(f"overall {new.overall:.1f}/100{overall_s}", overall_c)
    45→        + colorize(f"  objective {new.objective:.1f}/100{objective_s}", objective_c)
    46→        + colorize(f"  strict {new.strict:.1f}/100{strict_s}", strict_c)
    47→        + colorize(f"  verified {new.verified:.1f}/100{verified_s}", verified_c)
    48→    )
    49→
    50→    # Score-drop reassurance after structural fixes
    51→    if new.strict is not None and prev.strict is not None and new.strict < prev.strict:
    52→        print(colorize(
    53→            "  Score dropped — this is normal after structural fixes. "
    54→            "New issues may surface; keep working the queue.",
    55→            "yellow",
    56→        ))
    57→
    58→    # Always show strict target + next-command nudge
    59→    if config is None:
    60→        config = config_mod.load_config()
    61→
    62→    target = target_strict_score_from_config(config, fallback=95.0)
    63→    print_strict_target_nudge(new.strict, target)
    64→
    65→
    66→def print_strict_target_nudge(
    67→    strict: float, target: float, *, show_next: bool = True,
    68→) -> None:
    69→    """Print a one-liner with strict→target and optional next-command nudge."""
    70→    gap = round(target - strict, 1)
    71→    if gap > 0:
    72→        suffix = " — run `desloppify next` to find the next improvement" if show_next else ""
    73→        print(colorize(f"  Strict {strict:.1f} (target: {target:.1f}){suffix}", "dim"))
    74→    else:
    75→        print(colorize(f"  Strict {strict:.1f} — target {target:.1f} reached!", "green"))
    76→
    77→
    78→__all__ = ["print_score_update", "print_strict_target_nudge"]
    79→

    10→# Bump this integer whenever docs/SKILL.md changes in a way that agents
    11→# should pick up (new commands, changed workflows, removed sections).
    12→SKILL_VERSION = 3
    13→
    14→SKILL_VERSION_RE = re.compile(r"<!--\s*desloppify-skill-version:\s*(\d+)\s*-->")
    15→SKILL_OVERLAY_RE = re.compile(r"<!--\s*desloppify-overlay:\s*(\w+)\s*-->")
    16→
    17→SKILL_BEGIN = "<!-- desloppify-begin -->"
    18→SKILL_END = "<!-- desloppify-end -->"
    19→
    20→# Locations where the skill doc might be installed, relative to project root.
    21→SKILL_SEARCH_PATHS = (
    22→    ".claude/skills/desloppify/SKILL.md",
    23→    ".opencode/skills/desloppify/SKILL.md",
    24→    "AGENTS.md",
    25→    "CLAUDE.md",
    26→    ".cursor/rules/desloppify.md",
    27→    ".github/copilot-instructions.md",
    28→)
    29→
    30→# Interface name → (target file, overlay filename, dedicated).
    31→# Dedicated files are overwritten entirely; shared files get section replacement.
    32→SKILL_TARGETS: dict[str, tuple[str, str, bool]] = {
    33→    "claude": (".claude/skills/desloppify/SKILL.md", "CLAUDE", True),
    34→    # OpenCode support added with thanks to @H3xKatana.
    35→    "opencode": (".opencode/skills/desloppify/SKILL.md", "OPENCODE", True),
    36→    "codex": ("AGENTS.md", "CODEX", False),
    37→    "cursor": (".cursor/rules/desloppify.md", "CURSOR", True),
    38→    "copilot": (".github/copilot-instructions.md", "COPILOT", False),
    39→    "windsurf": ("AGENTS.md", "WINDSURF", False),
    40→    "gemini": ("AGENTS.md", "GEMINI", False),
    41→}
    42→
    43→
    44→@dataclass
    45→class SkillInstall:
    46→    """Detected skill document installation."""
    47→
    48→    rel_path: str
    49→    version: int
    50→    overlay: str | None
    51→    stale: bool
    52→
    53→
    54→def find_installed_skill() -> SkillInstall | None:
    55→    """Find installed skill document metadata, or None."""
    56→    project_root = get_project_root()
    57→    for rel_path in SKILL_SEARCH_PATHS:
    58→        full = project_root / rel_path
    59→        if not full.is_file():
    60→            continue
    61→        try:
    62→            content = full.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    63→        except OSError as exc:
    64→            _ = exc
    65→            continue
    66→        version_match = SKILL_VERSION_RE.search(content)
    67→        if not version_match:
    68→            continue
    69→        installed_version = int(version_match.group(1))
    70→        overlay_match = SKILL_OVERLAY_RE.search(content)
    71→        overlay = overlay_match.group(1) if overlay_match else None
    72→        return SkillInstall(
    73→            rel_path=rel_path,
    74→            version=installed_version,
    75→            overlay=overlay,
    76→            stale=installed_version < SKILL_VERSION,
    77→        )
    78→    return None
    79→
    80→
    81→def check_skill_version() -> str | None:
    82→    """Return a warning if installed skill doc is outdated."""
    83→    install = find_installed_skill()
    84→    if not install or not install.stale:
    85→        return None
    86→    return (
    87→        f"Your desloppify skill document is outdated "
    88→        f"(v{install.version}, current v{SKILL_VERSION}). "
    89→        "Run: desloppify update-skill"
    90→    )

1→"""Reusable CLI rendering snippets for command modules."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from collections.abc import Callable
     6→
     7→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.queue_progress import (
     8→    QueueBreakdown,
     9→    format_queue_headline,
    10→)
    11→from desloppify.base.discovery.api import rel
    12→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
    13→
    14→
    15→def print_agent_plan(
    16→    steps: list[str],
    17→    *,
    18→    next_command: str | None = None,
    19→    header: str = "  AGENT PLAN:",
    20→    plan: dict | None = None,
    21→) -> None:
    22→    """Print a consistent AGENT PLAN block with numbered steps.
    23→
    24→    When a living *plan* is active, renders plan focus/progress instead
    25→    of the narrative-derived steps.
    26→    """
    27→    if plan and (plan.get("queue_order") or plan.get("clusters")):
    28→        _print_plan_agent_block(plan, header=header)
    29→        return
    30→    if not steps:
    31→        return
    32→    print(colorize(header, "yellow"))
    33→    for idx, step in enumerate(steps, 1):
    34→        print(colorize(f"  {idx}. {step}", "dim"))
    35→    if next_command:
    36→        print(colorize(f"  Next command: `{next_command}`", "dim"))
    37→
    38→
    39→def _print_plan_agent_block(plan: dict, *, header: str = "  AGENT PLAN:") -> None:
    40→    """Render the living plan as the agent plan block."""
    41→    active = plan.get("active_cluster")
    42→    ordered = len(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    43→    skipped_ids = set(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
    44→    skipped = len(skipped_ids)
    45→    queue_order = plan.get("queue_order", [])
    46→    plan_ordered = sum(1 for fid in queue_order if fid not in skipped_ids)
    47→
    48→    # Build a lightweight breakdown for the headline
    49→    breakdown = QueueBreakdown(
    50→        queue_total=ordered,
    51→        plan_ordered=plan_ordered,
    52→        skipped=skipped,
    53→    )
    54→    headline = format_queue_headline(breakdown)
    55→
    56→    print(colorize(header, "yellow"))
    57→    print(colorize(f"  Living plan active: {headline}", "dim"))
    58→    if active:
    59→        cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(active, {})
    60→        remaining = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    61→        print(colorize(f"  Focused on: {active} ({remaining} items remaining).", "dim"))
    62→    print(colorize("  Next command: `desloppify next`", "dim"))
    63→    print(colorize("  View plan: `desloppify plan`", "dim"))
    64→
    65→
    66→def print_replacement_groups(
    67→    groups: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]],
    68→    *,
    69→    title: str,
    70→    rel_fn: Callable[[str], str] = rel,
    71→) -> None:
    72→    """Print grouped old→new replacement lines by file."""
    73→    if not groups:
    74→        return
    75→    print(colorize(title, "cyan"))
    76→    for filepath, replacements in sorted(groups.items()):
    77→        print(f"    {rel_fn(filepath)}:")
    78→        for old, new in replacements:
    79→            print(f"      {old}  →  {new}")
    80→    print()
    81→
    82→
    83→def print_ranked_actions(
    84→    actions: list[dict], *, limit: int = 3, plan: dict | None = None
    85→) -> bool:
    86→    """Print the highest-impact narrative actions and return True when shown."""
    87→    ranked = sorted(
    88→        [action for action in actions if int(action.get("count", 0)) > 0],
    89→        key=lambda action: (
    90→            -float(action.get("impact", 0.0)),
    91→            -int(action.get("count", 0)),
    92→            int(action.get("priority", 999)),
    93→        ),
    94→    )
    95→    if not ranked:
    96→        return False
    97→    has_plan = plan and (plan.get("queue_order") or plan.get("clusters"))
    98→    label = "Score context:" if has_plan else "Biggest things impacting score:"
    99→    print(colorize(f"  {label}", "cyan"))
   100→    for action in ranked[:limit]:
   101→        detector = action.get("detector", "unknown")
   102→        count = int(action.get("count", 0))
   103→        cluster_count = action.get("cluster_count")
   104→        if cluster_count:
   105→            print(colorize(f"    - {detector}: {count} open in {cluster_count} cluster(s) — `desloppify next`", "dim"))
   106→        else:
   107→            command = action.get("command", "desloppify next")
   108→            print(colorize(f"    - {detector}: {count} open — `{command}`", "dim"))
   109→    return True
   110→
   111→
   112→__all__ = [
   113→    "print_agent_plan",
   114→    "print_ranked_actions",
   115→    "print_replacement_groups",
   116→]

     5→
     6→def short_issue_id(fid: str) -> str:
     7→    """Extract the 8-char hash suffix from a issue ID for compact display.
     8→
     9→    Issue IDs look like ``review::.::holistic::dim::identifier::abcdef12``.
    10→    Commands accept the hash suffix as a shorthand for the full ID.
    11→    """
    12→    if "::" in fid:
    13→        suffix = fid.rsplit("::", 1)[-1]
    14→        if len(suffix) >= 8:
    15→            return suffix[:8]
    16→    return fid

    32→    exc: Exception,
    33→    *,
    34→    label: str = "output",
    35→) -> None:
    36→    """Print a standardized write-failure error for command output files."""
    37→    print_error(f"Could not write {label} to {path}: {exc}")
    38→
    39→
    40→def restore_files_best_effort(
    41→    snapshots: Mapping[str, str],
    42→    write_fn: Callable[[str, str], None],
    43→) -> list[str]:
    44→    """Attempt restoring a set of files and return paths that failed to restore."""
    45→    failed: list[str] = []
    46→    for filepath, original in snapshots.items():
    47→        try:
    48→            write_fn(filepath, original)
    49→        except OSError:
    50→            failed.append(filepath)
    51→    return failed
    52→
    53→
    54→__all__ = [
    55→    "log_best_effort_failure",
    56→    "print_error",
    57→    "print_write_error",
    58→    "restore_files_best_effort",
    59→    "warn_best_effort",
    60→]
    61→

     3→from __future__ import annotations

    17→def issue_weight(issue: dict) -> tuple[float, float, str]:

    19→    confidence = issue.get("confidence", "low")
    20→    is_holistic = issue.get("detail", {}).get("holistic", False)
    21→
    22→    weight = CONFIDENCE_WEIGHTS.get(confidence, 0.3)

    26→    return weight, weight, issue.get("id", "")
    27→
    28→
    29→def _append_assessment_context(

    31→) -> None:
    32→    if not subjective_assessments:

    34→
    35→    detail = issue.get("detail", {})

    53→

   144→    lines.append("```\n")

   147→def render_issue_detail(
   148→    issue: dict,
   149→    lang_name: str,
   150→    number: int | None = None,
   151→    subjective_assessments: dict | None = None,
   152→) -> str:
   153→    """Render one issue as a markdown work order from state."""
   154→    issue_id = issue["id"]
   155→    detail = issue.get("detail", {})
   156→    detector = issue.get("detector", "")
   157→    is_holistic = detail.get("holistic", False)
   158→    is_review = detector in ("review", "concerns")
   159→
   160→    # Derive dimension: from detail for review, from registry for mechanical.
   161→    raw_dimension = detail.get("dimension", "")
   162→    if raw_dimension:
   163→        dimension = raw_dimension.replace("_", " ")
   164→    else:
   165→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   166→        dimension = meta.dimension.replace("_", " ") if meta else "unknown"
   167→
   168→    confidence = issue.get("confidence", "low")
   169→
   170→    parts = issue_id.split("::")
   171→    identifier = parts[-2] if len(parts) >= 3 else issue.get("file", "unknown")
   172→    weight, impact_pts, _ = issue_weight(issue)
   173→    label = "+++" if weight >= 8 else "++" if weight >= 5 else "+"
   174→
   175→    lines: list[str] = []
   176→    lines.append(f"# {dimension}: {identifier}\n")
   177→    lines.append(f"**Issue**: `{issue_id}`  ")
   178→    if not is_review:
   179→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   180→        detector_display = meta.display if meta else detector
   181→        lines.append(f"**Detector**: {detector_display} | **Confidence**: {confidence}  ")
   182→    else:
   183→        lines.append(f"**Dimension**: {dimension} | **Confidence**: {confidence}  ")

   188→    lines.append("## Problem\n")

   191→    _append_evidence(lines, detail)

   193→    suggestion = detail.get("suggestion", "")
   194→    if suggestion:
   195→        lines.append("## Suggested Fix\n")
   196→        lines.append(f"{suggestion}\n")
   197→
   198→    _append_files(lines, issue, detail, is_holistic)
   199→
   200→    reasoning = detail.get("reasoning", "")
   201→    if reasoning:
   202→        lines.append("## Why This Matters\n")
   203→        lines.append(f"{reasoning}\n")
   204→
   205→    has_investigation = _append_investigation(lines, issue_id, detail)
   206→    _append_footer(

   209→        lang_name=lang_name,
   210→        issue_id=issue_id,
   211→        number=number,
   212→    )
   213→    return "\n".join(lines)
